definition_zh: 组织；纸巾；薄纸；薄纱；一套；一系列
definition_en: the material forming animal or plant cells; a soft paper for wiping; also a connected series of things
core_image: 显微镜下一层层细密的纤维，交织成薄薄的一片
scene: 实验台上放着一块刚染色的切片，细密的纹路层层叠叠。 Under the lens the tissue showed rows of round cells.
sceneCN: 这里 tissue 是「（生物）组织」（第 1 个义项：构成动植物体的细胞群）；句意为镜下组织呈现一排排圆形细胞。画面有切片、染色液与显微镜镜筒。

pos.zh: 名词：组织；纸巾；薄纸；一套

derivatives.zh: 加过去分词结尾，义为「薄的；织有金丝的」
加 -ar 构成，义为「组织的（医学用语）」

senses.title: Biological tissue
senses.definition: a group of similar cells in an animal or plant that performs a particular function
senses.definitionCN: 动植物体内功能相近的一群细胞
senses.example: Muscle tissue responds to nerve signals.
senses.exampleCN: 肌肉组织对神经信号作出反应。
senses.why: The word comes from the Latin for woven cloth, and cells woven together form a tissue.
senses.whyCN: 本词来自拉丁语「织物」，细胞交织成片就成了组织。

senses.title: Soft paper
senses.definition: soft absorbent paper used for wiping or wrapping
senses.definitionCN: 用于擦拭或包装的柔软吸水性纸
senses.example: She handed him a tissue for his cold.
senses.exampleCN: 他有鼻炎，她递给他一张纸巾。
senses.why: Thin paper is made of interlaced fibres, so the cloth image fits the paper exactly.
senses.whyCN: 薄纸由交错纤维制成，织物意象正好贴合。

senses.title: Thin woven cloth
senses.definition: a very thin, fine cloth, often with metallic threads
senses.definitionCN: 极薄细致的织物，常带金属丝
senses.example: The dress was trimmed with silver tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这件裙子镶着银线薄纱。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense, woven fabric with a visible interlaced pattern.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的直义，即可见交织纹理的织物。

senses.title: A connected series
senses.definition: a series of related statements or events
senses.definitionCN: 相互关联的一系列说法或事件
senses.example: The report was a tissue of unverified claims.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是一连串未经核实的说法。
senses.why: Things woven together also form a connected whole, so a chain of claims can be a tissue.
senses.whyCN: 交织之物也成相连的整体，因此一连串说法也可称 tissue。

senses.title: Wrapping paper
senses.definition: light paper used to wrap delicate goods or line boxes
senses.definitionCN: 包装易碎品或衬箱的薄纸
senses.example: The glasses were wrapped in tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃杯用薄纸包了起来。
senses.why: The paper sense narrows to the specific task of protecting fragile things.
senses.whyCN: 纸的意义收窄到保护易碎物的具体用途。

senses.title: Toilet tissue
senses.definition: the soft paper used in bathrooms, in the fixed phrase toilet tissue
senses.definitionCN: 浴室用软纸，见于 toilet tissue 这一固定搭配
senses.example: The hotel replaced the toilet tissue every day.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店每天都换卫生纸。
senses.why: The material sense fixes into a household product name.
senses.whyCN: 材料义固定成了家庭用品的名称。

senses.title: Nervous tissue
senses.definition: the specialised tissue of nerves and nerve cells
senses.definitionCN: 由神经与神经细胞构成的特化组织
senses.example: Nervous tissue conducts signals through the body.
senses.exampleCN: 神经组织在体内传导信号。
senses.why: Every kind of body tissue takes the name, so the word multiplies across anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 身体各组织都可用这个词，于是它在解剖学中不断派生。

senses.title: A fibrous network
senses.definition: any interwoven network of fibres or fine lines
senses.definitionCN: 任何交织的纤维或细线结构
senses.example: A fine tissue of roots covered the stone.
senses.exampleCN: 一层细密的根须网络覆在石上。
senses.why: From cloth to cells to roots, the constant is the interwoven pattern.
senses.whyCN: 从布到细胞再到根，共同点就是交织的纹理。

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin for woven cloth, passes through French, and is extended to biology once microscopy shows tissue as a woven material.
intro.cn: 本词来自拉丁语「织成的布」，经法语进入英语，显微镜把生物组织看作织成品后，词义便延伸到生物学。

items.en: Texere meant to weave, and textile is its participle describing what is woven.
items.cn: texere 意为「编织」，textile 是表示「织成的」的分词。

items.en: Tissu, the French participle of weaving, named a woven fabric.
items.cn: tissu 是法语的分词形式，指织成的布。

items.en: Tissue enters English naming a rich cloth woven with gold or silver thread.
items.cn: tissue 进入英语时指织有金银线的华贵织物。

items.en: The sense widens to any light woven material and then to thin paper.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何轻薄织品，再扩展到薄纸。

items.en: In the seventeenth century tissue takes on the meaning of a connected series.
items.cn: 十七世纪 tissue 获得「相连的一串」之义。

items.en: Biology adopts the word for cells woven together as a tissue.
items.cn: 生物学把本词用于交织成片的细胞。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers textile words from the same weaving root, and the near-meaning group lists related paper and biology words.
note.cn: 形近组收集同出「编织」词根的纺织类词，近义组列出相关的纸与生物词。

entries.definition: the feel or arrangement of a surface
woven cloth or the industry that makes it
thin, or woven with gold thread
an older spelling of tissue, now obsolete
material made from pressed fibres
a cloth or paper for wiping the mouth
the soft substance of a body
a thin layer covering or lining tissue

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the weaving root, the cloth-to-paper path, and the biology extension.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从「编织」词根、由布到纸的路径与生物学延伸入手。

normal.en: Tissue and textile share the Latin weave, so tissue is anything woven into a sheet.
normal.cn: tissue 与 textile 同出拉丁语「编织」，凡织成片的东西都可称 tissue。

normal.en: Cells woven together make body tissue, just as threads woven together make cloth.
normal.cn: 细胞交织成组织，正如线交织成布。

normal.en: A tissue of lies is a fabric of lies, the oldest cloth image kept.
normal.cn: a tissue of lies 就是谎言的织物，保留了最古老的布意象。

normal.en: Tissue paper is the paper that most clearly shows its fibre network.
normal.cn: tissue paper 最能看出纤维交织的纸。

normal.en: Muscle, nervous, and plant tissue are the three phrases to start with.
normal.cn: muscle、nervous、plant tissue 是最先该记的三个短语。

abstract.en: Picture threads crossing in a loom until a flat sheet appears.
abstract.cn: 想象织机上来回穿梭的线，渐渐成了平薄的一片。

abstract.en: Think of a microscope turning mottled colour into rows of round cells.
abstract.cn: 想显微镜把杂色看成一排排圆细胞。

abstract.en: A thin paper tissue is cloth made far finer than you can feel.
abstract.cn: 一张薄纸巾就是细得摸不出纹理的布。

examples.en: The surgeon removed a small area of damaged tissue.
examples.cn: 外科医生切除了一小块受损组织。

examples.en: He took a tissue from the box and wiped the table.
examples.cn: 他从盒里取了一张纸巾擦桌子。

examples.en: The story turned out to be a tissue of excuses.
examples.cn: 这件事最后被证明是一连串借口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提湿」——提起湿纸巾，薄得透光。

root: 拉丁语 texere（编织）的分词 textile 经古法语 tissu 进入英语，本义「织物」，后指薄纸；十七世纪起引申为「相连的一串」，生物学用来指交织成片的细胞。

sensesIntro.en: Weaving is the constant: cloth, then paper, then cells, then the network of roots, and even a chain of statements is woven, while the biology sense now stands first.
sensesIntro.cn: 「编织」是常量：布、纸、细胞、根须网络，乃至一连串说法都是织成的；如今头义已是生物学义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many fine threads crossing into one thin flat sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多细线交错成薄薄的一片。

branches.en: Cells woven into a bodily layer.
branches.cn: 细胞交织成的身体层次。

branches.en: Paper made of fine fibres.
branches.cn: 由细纤维制成的纸。

branches.en: The literal woven fabric.
branches.cn: 字面的织物。

branches.en: A woven series of statements.
branches.cn: 织成一串的言论。

branches.en: Any visible network of fibres.
branches.cn: 任何可见的纤维网络。

intro.en: The stem comes from the Latin weave, so the affix work pairs that root with the endings found in its family.
intro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语「编织」，构词要点是把该词根与词族中的词尾配合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin list gives the weaving root itself and the borrowed forms built on it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁表给出「编织」词根本身以及建在其上的借入形式。

items.example: Tissue is literally what is woven.
items.exampleCN: tissue 字面就是「被织成的东西」。

items.example: Old French tissu keeps this ending.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 tissu 保留了这个词尾。

items.example: Tissues covers many kinds of cells.
Tissue paper is the soft wrapping paper.
items.exampleCN: tissue paper 是柔软的包装纸。

items.example: A tissue box sits on every desk.
items.exampleCN: tissue box 摆在每张桌上。

definition_zh: 酶；催化生物化学反应、通常为蛋白质（少数为 RNA）的分子
definition_en: a molecule, usually a protein and sometimes an RNA, that speeds up a biochemical reaction without being consumed by it
core_image: 一把带凹槽的钥匙插进锁孔，锁一开，原本卡住的部件立刻分开，钥匙本身完好退出
scene: 这里指「酶」。 One enzyme in saliva begins breaking starch into sugars before the food has even been swallowed.
sceneCN: 这里 enzyme 指「酶」这一催化分子（第 1 个义项：催化生化反应而自身不被消耗的分子）；唾液中的酶在食物下咽前就开始把淀粉切成糖。图中可辨识物件：带凹槽的钥匙、锁孔、分开的部件、完好的钥匙。

senses.title: The catalyst itself
senses.definition: a molecule that catalyses a biochemical reaction and is not consumed by it
senses.definitionCN: 催化生化反应而自身不被消耗的分子
senses.example: Each enzyme in the pathway is named for the reaction it runs.
senses.exampleCN: 通路中的每一种酶都按它催化的反应命名。
senses.why: Greek en- 'in' plus zymē 'leaven' produced a name for something inside yeast that drives change, and that name now labels the catalyst itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 en-「在内」加 zymē「酵素」造出一个名称，指酵母中驱动变化的东西，后来这个名称就指催化剂本身。

senses.title: Lowering the barrier
senses.titleCN: 催化作用：降低反应门槛
senses.definition: the catalytic act of lowering the activation energy so a reaction runs at body temperature
senses.definitionCN: 降低活化能、使反应能在体温下进行的作用
senses.example: Without the enzyme, the reaction would take hours instead of seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 没有这种酶，反应要数小时而不是数秒。
senses.why: the name originally marked what happens inside yeast, so the word also names the speeding up rather than the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字最初标记酵母内部发生的事，因此它也能指「加快反应」这一动作，而非物体。

senses.title: One substrate, one reaction
senses.definition: the specificity of an enzyme for a particular substrate or a particular bond
senses.definitionCN: 酶只对特定底物或特定化学键起作用
senses.example: A protease will not touch a sugar, however similar the shape.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白酶不会去碰糖，无论形状多相似。
senses.why: the active site is a shaped pocket, so specificity follows directly from the geometry of the catalyst.
senses.whyCN: 活性位点是一个有形状的口袋，因此专一性直接来自催化剂的几何形状。

senses.title: The shaped pocket
senses.titleCN: 活性位点：口袋与结合面
senses.definition: the region of the enzyme where the substrate binds and the reaction occurs
senses.definitionCN: 酶上与底物结合并发生反应的区域
senses.example: The active site holds the substrate in the one orientation that reacts.
senses.exampleCN: 活性位点把底物固定在唯一能反应的方向上。
senses.why: if the catalyst is a pocket, the pocket is the part that does the work, so the word extends to that region.
senses.whyCN: 如果催化剂是一个口袋，起作用的就是口袋本身，于是这个词也延伸到该区域。

senses.title: Rates and curves
senses.titleCN: 酶促动力学：速率与曲线
senses.definition: the quantitative study of how fast an enzyme works as substrate concentration rises
senses.definitionCN: 研究底物浓度升高时酶工作速率的定量描述
senses.example: The enzyme reaches half its maximum rate at a characteristic substrate level.
senses.exampleCN: 该酶在某一特征底物浓度下达到最大速率的一半。
senses.why: because enzymes are catalysts, measuring them means measuring rates, and the word carries that quantitative sense.
senses.whyCN: 由于酶是催化剂，研究它就是测速率，这个词也带上这种定量含义。

senses.title: Named with -ase
senses.titleCN: 命名与分类：以 -ase 结尾
senses.definition: an enzyme named by adding -ase to the substrate or the reaction, as in protease or dehydrogenase
senses.definitionCN: 在底物或反应名后加 -ase 构成的酶名，如蛋白酶、脱氢酶
senses.example: The ending -ase tells you at a glance that the word is an enzyme.
senses.exampleCN: -ase 结尾一眼就能看出这个词是酶。
senses.why: once the class had a naming rule, the suffix became part of what the word means.
senses.whyCN: 当这一类有了命名规则，后缀本身就成了词义的一部分。

senses.title: Blocked on purpose
senses.titleCN: 抑制与调控：被有意阻断
senses.definition: the enzyme as a target of inhibitors and of cellular regulation
senses.definitionCN: 酶作为抑制剂与细胞调控的靶点
senses.example: Statins inhibit the enzyme that makes cholesterol.
senses.exampleCN: 他汀类药物抑制制造胆固醇的酶。
senses.why: because a catalyst can be jammed, medicine and physiology read the word as something to switch off.
senses.whyCN: 由于催化剂可以被卡住，医学与生理学把这个词读成「可以关掉的东西」。

senses.title: Working outside a cell
senses.definition: an enzyme used as a tool in industry, food processing or therapy
senses.definitionCN: 在工业、食品加工或治疗中作为工具使用的酶
senses.example: Laundry detergents contain an enzyme that digests protein stains.
senses.exampleCN: 洗衣剂含有能分解蛋白污渍的酶。
senses.why: purified catalysts can be put to work outside the body, so the word also names a commercial and clinical tool.
senses.whyCN: 纯化后的催化剂可在体外工作，因此这个词也指一种商品与临床工具。

intro.en: Enzyme was coined in 1877 from Greek en- 'in' and zymē 'leaven, ferment'. It replaced the older word ferment for the agent rather than the process.
intro.cn: enzyme 于 1877 年由希腊 en-「在内」与 zymē「酵素、发酵剂」造出；它取代了较早的 ferment，用来指作用者而非过程。

items.en: zymē meant leaven or ferment, the stuff that makes dough rise and juice turn. The word is old in Greek and its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: zymē 指酵素或发酵剂，是让面团发起、果汁变味的东西。该词在希腊语中很古老，更深来源无定论。

items.en: Wilhelm Kühne proposed Enzyme in 1877 to name the agent responsible for fermentation, separating it from the process.
items.cn: Wilhelm Kühne 于 1877 年提出 Enzyme，用来命名负责发酵的作用者，把它与过程区分开。

items.en: Generally thought: the name means 'in yeast', because the fermenting agent was first studied in yeast extracts; Kühne's fuller argument is not documented in detail.
items.cn: 一般认为是：「在酵母中」之意，因为发酵作用者最早在酵母提取物中被研究；Kühne 更完整的论证并无详细记录。

items.en: English took enzyme in the late nineteenth century and dropped ferment for the agent; the first citation is approximate.
items.cn: 英语于 19 世纪后期吸收 enzyme，并用它取代 ferment 指作用者；最早书证年代为约数。

items.en: Twentieth-century biochemistry showed most enzymes are proteins and some are catalytic RNA, widening the definition.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生物化学表明多数酶是蛋白质，少数是催化性 RNA，从而拓宽了定义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): zymē has no agreed pre-Greek origin, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：zymē 在希腊语之前的来源并无共识，其背后的任何印欧形式都是重构，而不是有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds words sharing the Greek zymē stem or the enzyme label but naming different things; group two holds the words of the reaction it runs.
note.cn: 第一组是共享希腊 zymē 词干或酶标签、但指不同事物的词；第二组是它所催化反应中的相关词。

entries.definition: The adjective 'of an enzyme'. It describes a reaction or a assay, never the catalyst as a countable object.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词「酶的」，描述反应或测定，不能作可数名词指催化剂本身。

entries.definition: A small molecule that assists an enzyme, such as NAD. It is not itself the protein catalyst.
entries.definitionCN: 指辅助酶的小分子，如 NAD；它本身不是蛋白催化剂。

entries.definition: An inactive form of an enzyme, built with -gen 'producing'. It must be cut before it works.
entries.definitionCN: 酶的失活前体，由 -gen「产生」构成；必须被切割后才能工作。

entries.definition: The study of enzymes, with -logy 'study'. It names a field of research.
entries.definitionCN: 研究酶的学科，由 -logy「学科」构成；指研究领域。

entries.definition: Any agent that speeds a reaction without being consumed; an enzyme is one kind of catalyst, and inorganic ones also exist.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指加快反应而自身不被消耗的作用者；酶是其中一类，也存在无机催化剂。

entries.definition: The molecule an enzyme works on. The enzyme is the tool; the substrate is the material.
entries.definitionCN: 指酶所作用的分子；酶是工具，底物是材料。

entries.definition: A non-protein substance, ion or small molecule, needed for activity. It assists rather than catalyses alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指活性所必需的非蛋白物质、离子或小分子；它辅助而非单独催化。

entries.definition: A protein-cutting enzyme, named with -ase. It is a member of the enzyme class, not the class itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指切割蛋白质的酶，由 -ase 构成；是酶类中的一员，而非该类整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: en- 'in' + zymē 'leaven': the leaven inside the cell.
normal.cn: en-「在内」+ zymē「酵素」：细胞里的那点「酵」。

normal.en: The family runs enzyme, enzymatic, enzymic, enzymology, coenzyme, zymogen.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 enzyme、enzymatic、enzymic、enzymology、coenzyme、zymogen。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: digestive enzyme, enzyme activity, enzyme inhibitor, immobilized enzyme.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：消化酶、酶活性、酶抑制剂、固定化酶。

normal.en: Class naming rule: substrate or reaction plus -ase, as in protease and dehydrogenase.
normal.cn: 类别命名规则：底物或反应加 -ase，如蛋白酶、脱氢酶。

normal.en: An enzyme is a key, the substrate is the lock, and the reaction is the door opening.
normal.cn: 酶是钥匙，底物是锁，反应是门被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a key that leaves the lock exactly as it found it, ready for the next turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙开完锁后原样退出，等待下一次转动。

abstract.en: Picture a workbench whose dent fits one part and no other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工作台，其凹槽只容得下一种零件。

abstract.en: Picture a factory that can be shut down by jamming a single station.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂，卡住一个工位就能让它停工。

examples.en: The enzyme is reusable, so a small amount handles a large batch.
examples.cn: 这种酶可重复使用，少量即可处理一大批。

examples.en: Heat denatures the enzyme and the reaction stops.
examples.cn: 高温使酶变性，反应随之中止。

examples.en: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences.
examples.cn: 限制性内切酶在特定序列处切割 DNA。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「按（en）在酵（zyme）里」——细胞里那点让反应跑起来的「酵」 → 酶

root: 希腊 en-「在内」+ zymē「酵素、发酵剂」→ 德语 Enzyme（1877，Kühne 提议）→ 英语 enzyme。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a shaped key enters a lock, turns, leaves unchanged, and the door opens; that movement is then read as the agent, the speeding up, the fit, the pocket, the rate, the naming rule, the jammed lock, and the tool sold outside.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一把有形状的钥匙进锁、转动、原样退出，门随之打开；这一动作依次被读成作用者、加速、契合、口袋、速率、命名规则、被卡住的锁，以及卖到体外的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shaped key entering a lock, turning, and leaving exactly as it came.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把有形状的钥匙进锁、转动，原样退出。

branches.en: THE AGENT: the key itself, named for what happens inside yeast.
branches.cn: 作用者：钥匙本身，因酵母内部发生的事而得名。

branches.en: THE TURN: catalysis, the barrier lowered so the door opens.
branches.cn: 转动：催化，门槛降低使门打开。

branches.en: THE FIT: specificity and the pocket that makes it.
branches.cn: 契合：专一性，以及造成专一性的口袋。

branches.en: MEASURE AND NAME: rates and curves, and the -ase rule that labels the class.
branches.cn: 测量与命名：速率与曲线，以及标记该类的 -ase 规则。

branches.en: JAM AND EXPORT: a target to block, and a purified tool put to work outside the cell.
branches.cn: 卡住与外用：可被阻断的靶点，以及纯化后在胞外工作的工具。

intro.en: Enzyme is a Greek compound of a preposition and a noun; the English family adds Latin -aticus and Greek -logia as well as the modern -ase.
intro.cn: enzyme 是希腊介词与名词的合成词；英语词族另加拉丁 -aticus、希腊 -logia 以及现代的 -ase。

latinIntro.en: There is no classical Latin source. New Latin enzyma is a Latinized spelling, and -aticus is the Latin suffix that yields English -atic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有古典拉丁来源。新拉丁语 enzyma 是拉丁化拼写；-aticus 是产生英语 -atic 的拉丁后缀。

items.example: The enzyme remains active at thirty-seven degrees.
items.exampleCN: 该酶在三十七度下保持活性。
唾液中的酶开始消化淀粉。

items.meaning: of an enzyme; carried out by one
items.example: The reaction is enzymatic, not spontaneous.
items.exampleCN: 该反应是酶促的，不是自发的。

items.example: Enzymology grew out of fermentation research.
items.exampleCN: 酶学从发酵研究中成长起来。

items.example: NAD acts as a coenzyme in oxidation.
Trypsinogen is a zymogen of trypsin.
items.exampleCN: 胰蛋白酶原是一种酶原。

items.example: A protease removes the signal peptide.
Dehydrogenase feeds electrons into the chain.
items.exampleCN: 脱氢酶把电子送入传递链。

items.meaning: attached to an enzyme for detection
items.example: An enzyme-linked assay measured the hormone.
items.exampleCN: 一种酶联测定法测量了该激素。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to, of the nature of

definition_en: a protein made by the immune system that recognises and binds to a specific foreign substance
core_image: 一个 Y 形的蛋白分子用两个臂抓住一个病毒表面的突起
scene: 免疫系统记住了那次感染，下次就能立刻认出病毒。 The antibody binds to the virus and marks it for destruction.
sceneCN: 这里 antibody 指「抗体」（第 1 个义项：免疫系统产生、能识别并结合特定异物的蛋白）；句意：抗体结合到病毒上，并把它标记为待清除对象。图中可辨识物件：Y 形蛋白分子、病毒颗粒、结合位点、免疫细胞。

pos.zh: 抗体；免疫球蛋白（能识别并结合特定抗原的蛋白）

senses.title: Immune binding protein
senses.titleCN: 抗体：免疫系统产生、能特异结合的蛋白
senses.definition: a protein produced by immune cells that recognises a specific foreign molecule and binds to it
senses.definitionCN: 免疫细胞产生、能识别特定异物分子并与之结合的蛋白质
senses.example: The antibody binds to the virus and marks it for destruction.
senses.exampleCN: 抗体结合到病毒上，并把它标记为待清除对象。
senses.why: The name is a literal translation of German Antikörper, 'against-body': the substance made against the foreign body that entered.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字是德语 Antikörper「对抗外来体」的直译：针对进入体内的异物而造出的物质。

senses.title: A specific antibody
senses.titleCN: 某一种抗体：针对某一抗原的那一个
senses.definition: one particular antibody directed at one antigen, often named after its target
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一抗原的一种抗体，常以其目标命名
senses.example: Doctors looked for antibodies to the measles virus in her blood.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在她的血液中寻找针对麻疹病毒的抗体。
senses.why: Each antibody has a unique binding site, so the general word is constantly used for a single member of the family, named by its target.
senses.whyCN: 每个抗体都有独特的结合位点，因此这个总称常被用来指家族中的一个具体成员，并以目标命名。

senses.title: Neutralizing antibody
senses.titleCN: 中和抗体：结合后使病原失去感染力
senses.definition: an antibody that blocks a virus or toxin from entering cells or doing harm
senses.definitionCN: 结合后阻止病毒或毒素进入细胞或造成伤害的抗体
senses.example: A neutralizing antibody can stop the virus before it enters a cell.
senses.exampleCN: 中和抗体能在病毒进入细胞之前把它拦住。
senses.why: Binding alone is not always enough; some antibodies physically cover the entry site, and that functional result earned its own name.
senses.whyCN: 仅仅结合未必够用；有些抗体物理地遮住进入位点，这一功能结果便获得了专名。

senses.title: Monoclonal antibody
senses.titleCN: 单克隆抗体：来自单一细胞系、结构一致
senses.definition: a laboratory-made antibody produced from one cell line, so that every copy is identical
senses.definitionCN: 由单一细胞系产生的实验室抗体，每一份拷贝都相同
senses.example: The monoclonal antibody is used in both tests and cancer treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这种单克隆抗体既用于检测，也用于癌症治疗。
senses.why: Natural antibodies are a mixture; cloning one cell line makes a single reagent, and industry needed a term for that uniformity.
senses.whyCN: 天然抗体是混合物；克隆一个细胞系可得到单一试剂，产业需要为这种一致性造一个术语。

senses.title: Polyclonal antibody
senses.titleCN: 多克隆抗体：来自多种细胞、识别多个位点
senses.definition: an antibody preparation containing many different antibodies that recognise different parts of the same target
senses.definitionCN: 含多种抗体、识别同一目标不同部位的抗体制品
senses.example: The polyclonal antibody still works when the virus mutates.
senses.exampleCN: 即使病毒变异，这种多克隆抗体仍然有效。
senses.why: An animal immunised against a whole germ makes many antibodies at once, and that breadth is useful precisely where a single clone would fail.
senses.whyCN: 用整个病原免疫动物会一次产生许多抗体，这种广度恰在单一克隆失效之处有用。

senses.title: Autoantibody
senses.titleCN: 自身抗体：攻击自身组织的抗体
senses.definition: an antibody that recognises the body's own tissue and attacks it, causing autoimmune disease
senses.definitionCN: 识别并攻击自身组织的抗体，引起自身免疫病
senses.example: Autoantibodies against the thyroid explain her fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 针对甲状腺的自身抗体解释了她的疲乏。
senses.why: The mechanism is the same as against a germ; only the target is wrong, so a prefix rather than a new word marks the pathology.
senses.whyCN: 机制与对抗病原完全相同，只是目标错了，因此用前缀而不是新词来标记这种病理。

senses.title: Antibody titre
senses.titleCN: 抗体滴度：以稀释倍数表示的抗体浓度
senses.definition: the amount of a particular antibody in the blood, usually expressed as the highest dilution that still gives a positive test
senses.definitionCN: 血中某种抗体的量，通常以仍呈阳性结果的最高稀释倍数表示
senses.example: Her antibody titre rose sharply after the second dose.
senses.exampleCN: 第二剂之后她的抗体滴度大幅上升。
senses.why: Because antibodies act by binding, their usefulness is a matter of how much is present, and dilution is the practical way to measure that.
senses.whyCN: 抗体的作用靠结合，因此其有用性取决于存在多少，而稀释是测量这个量的实用方法。

senses.title: Antibody as reagent
senses.titleCN: 抗体试剂：检测中用来抓取目标分子
senses.definition: an antibody used in the laboratory as a tool to detect, label or separate the molecule it binds
senses.definitionCN: 实验室中用来检测、标记或分离其所结合分子的抗体工具
senses.example: The antibody was conjugated to a dye for the pregnancy test.
senses.exampleCN: 这种抗体被接上染料，用于妊娠检测。
senses.why: Specific binding is a targeting mechanism, so the same molecule that defends a body can be used to find a substance on a plastic strip.
senses.whyCN: 特异结合是一种定位机制，因此同一个保卫身体的分子也能被用来在塑料试纸条上找到某种物质。

intro.en: Antibody is an English loan translation of German Antikörper, coined in the age of serum research: anti- 'against' plus body, the foreign body that the substance works against.
intro.cn: antibody 是德语 Antikörper 的英语仿译，造于血清研究时代：anti-「对抗」加 body，即该物质所对抗的外来体。

items.en: Greek anti meant 'against, instead of', and English uses it in hundreds of words for opposition or counteraction.
items.cn: 希腊 anti 意为「对抗、代替」，英语用它造出大量表示对抗或反作用的词。

items.en: In the 1890s researchers found that blood serum could neutralise toxins and bacteria, and that the effect could be transferred from one animal to another.
items.cn: 1890 年代研究者发现血清能中和毒素与细菌，而且这种效应可从一只动物转移到另一只。

items.en: Paul Ehrlich and others described the active substances as substances formed against a foreign body, and German named them Antikörper.
items.cn: 保罗·埃利希等人把这些活性物质描述为针对外来体而形成的物质，德语称之为 Antikörper。

items.en: English rendered the German compound piece by piece as antibody, first in the 1890s, keeping the literal structure of the original.
items.cn: 英语把德语复合词逐部件译成 antibody，最早见于 1890 年代，保留了原词的字面结构。

items.en: When the chemistry of these proteins was worked out in the twentieth century, the neutral term immunoglobulin was added, and the two words now name the same class from different angles.
items.cn: 20 世纪弄清这些蛋白的化学结构后，又加入了中性的 immunoglobulin 一词；今天两个词从不同角度命名同一类分子。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact English first date and the precise share of credit between Ehrlich and his contemporaries are not firmly fixed; the 1891 attribution usually given is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与归属存疑）：antibody 的英语确切首见年代、以及埃利希与同代人之间应得的贡献比例都无定论；通常所说的 1891 年只是约数。

note.en: The first group holds the partner terms and look-alikes built from anti-; the second holds the immune proteins and preparations that are easily mistaken for an antibody.
note.cn: 第一组是配对术语与用 anti- 构成的形近词；第二组是容易与抗体混淆的免疫蛋白与制品。

entries.definition: The foreign substance that an antibody binds; antigen ends in -gen 'producing', antibody ends in body.
entries.definitionCN: 抗体所结合的异物；antigen 以 -gen「产生」结尾，antibody 以 body 结尾。

entries.definition: A drug that kills bacteria, from anti- plus Greek bios 'life'; it acts on the germ, not on the immune system.
entries.definitionCN: 杀灭细菌的药物，来自 anti- 加希腊 bios「生命」；它作用于病原而非免疫系统。

entries.definition: Blood serum containing antibodies, used as a treatment; it is a container of antibodies, not one antibody.
entries.definitionCN: 含抗体的血清制品，用作治疗；它是抗体的容器，而不是单个抗体。

entries.definition: The protein class to which antibodies belong; the two words overlap almost completely but differ in register.
entries.definitionCN: 抗体所属的蛋白类别；两个词几乎完全重叠，只是语体不同。

entries.definition: The protection itself; antibodies are one of the means by which immunity is achieved.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护状态本身；抗体是实现免疫的手段之一。

entries.definition: A preparation that trains the body to make antibodies; it contains antigens rather than antibodies.
entries.definitionCN: 训练身体产生抗体的制品；它含的是抗原而不是抗体。

entries.definition: A white blood cell that kills infected cells directly; it acts by contact rather than by secreted binding proteins.
entries.definitionCN: 直接杀死受感染细胞的白细胞；它靠接触而非分泌结合蛋白发挥作用。

entries.definition: A molecule on a cell surface that binds a specific substance; it shares the binding function but is not made against a germ.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞表面结合特定物质的分子；共享结合功能，但不是针对病原而造。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: anti- 'against' + body 'foreign body' gives 'the thing made against the invader'.
normal.cn: anti-「对抗」+ body「外来体」得出「针对入侵者造出的东西」。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: antigen is the target, antibody is the defender.
normal.cn: 这一对是固定的：antigen 是目标，antibody 是防御者。

normal.en: The family runs antibody, antigen, antiserum, autoantibody and immunoglobulin.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 antibody、antigen、antiserum、autoantibody、immunoglobulin。

normal.en: Y-shaped with two arms: each arm is one binding site, which is why one antibody can grip two targets.
normal.cn: Y 形有两个臂，每个臂一个结合位点，因此一个抗体能抓住两个目标。

normal.en: monoclonal means one clone, polyclonal means many clones.
normal.cn: monoclonal 指单一克隆，polyclonal 指多克隆。

abstract.en: Picture a molecular hand that fits one lock and no other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只分子之手，只配一把锁，别的一概不配。

abstract.en: Picture a tag attached to an intruder so the guards can see it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签贴到入侵者身上，让守卫看得见。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line where every copy of one tool is identical.
abstract.cn: 想象一条生产线，同一件工具的每一份都一模一样。

examples.en: Antibodies appear in the blood a week or two after infection.
examples.cn: 感染后一两周，血液中会出现抗体。

examples.en: Monoclonal antibodies are grown in tanks rather than taken from people.
examples.cn: 单克隆抗体在罐中培养，而不是从人体中提取。

examples.en: The antibody test shows past exposure, not current infection.
examples.cn: 抗体检测显示的是既往接触，而不是当前感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「anti 对抗 + body 身体（外来体）」——针对外来体造出的蛋白 → antibody 抗体

root: 希腊 anti「对抗」+ 英语 body「体」→ 仿译德语 Antikörper → 英语 antibody（1890 年代）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one Y-shaped grip: the class of binding proteins, one member of it, the neutralizing and monoclonal and polyclonal forms, the misdirected autoantibody, its measured amount, and its use as a lab reagent.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个 Y 形抓握展开：这一类结合蛋白、其中一个成员、中和型与单克隆型及多克隆型、瞄错目标的自身抗体、它的测定量，以及它作为实验室试剂的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a Y-shaped protein whose two arms lock onto a germ's surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个 Y 形蛋白，两个臂锁住病原表面。

branches.en: CLASS AND MEMBER: the whole family of binding proteins, then a single named one.
branches.cn: 类别与成员：整个结合蛋白家族，然后是单个有名字的成员。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND MANUFACTURE: some antibodies block entry, others are grown as identical reagents.
branches.cn: 功能与制造：有些抗体封住入口，有些则被培养成一致的试剂。

branches.en: BREADTH: a polyclonal mixture covers many sites where one clone cannot.
branches.cn: 广度：多克隆混合物覆盖单一克隆覆盖不了的多个位点。

branches.en: WRONG TARGET AND NUMBER: against the self it causes disease, and its amount is measured by dilution.
branches.cn: 错误目标与数量：针对自身时致病，其多少用稀释测定。

branches.en: OUT OF THE BODY: specific binding becomes a detection tool on a test strip.
branches.cn: 离开身体：特异结合变成试纸条上的检测工具。

intro.en: Antibody is a two-word compound fused into one: anti- 'against' plus body. Its relatives are built by adding prefixes such as auto- and mono-.
intro.cn: antibody 是两个词融合成的复合词：anti-「对抗」加 body。同族词靠加 auto-、mono- 等前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The anti- element is Greek; the body element is English. The word is a modern scientific compound rather than a Latin inheritance, and it mirrors German Antikörper.
latinIntro.cn: anti- 成分来自希腊语，body 成分是英语。这个词是现代科学复合词，而非拉丁语继承，它对应德语 Antikörper。

items.meaning: a protein made against a foreign substance
items.example: One antibody can bind two virus particles.
items.exampleCN: 一个抗体能结合两个病毒颗粒。

items.example: Antibodies persist for years after measles.
items.exampleCN: 麻疹后抗体可持续多年。

items.meaning: the substance that makes antibodies be produced
items.example: The spike protein is the main antigen.

items.exampleCN: 自身抗体损伤关节内衬。
单克隆抗体是完全相同的拷贝。
多克隆血清含多种抗体。

items.example: Antiserum was given against the snake venom.
items.exampleCN: 针对蛇毒给予了抗血清。

items.example: IgG is the most common immunoglobulin.
items.exampleCN: IgG 是最常见的免疫球蛋白。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 身体；实体（英语 body 的拉丁对应词，用于说明 body 一词的来源）
对抗；相对（拉丁语中与希腊 anti 语义对应）

definition_zh: 细菌（bacterium 的复数）；细菌界；细菌（作为一大类微生物）
definition_en: the plural of bacterium, naming single-celled organisms without a nucleus, many of which live in soil, water, food and bodies
core_image: 显微镜下密密麻麻的微小杆状、球状细胞，没有细胞核
scene: 这里指「细菌的复数」。 Bacteria in the gut help break down food that the body cannot digest alone.
sceneCN: 这里 bacteria 指「细菌」（第 2 个义项：生活在肠道等特定环境中的细菌群）；句意：肠道里的细菌帮助分解身体无法独自消化的食物。图中可辨识物件：显微镜视野、杆状与球状菌体、肠道内壁、食物颗粒。

pos.zh: 细菌（bacterium 的复数形式，常作复数名词使用）

senses.title: Plural of bacterium
senses.titleCN: 细菌：bacterium 的复数，单细胞原核生物
senses.definition: the plural of bacterium: single-celled organisms that have no nucleus and reproduce by dividing
senses.definitionCN: bacterium 的复数：没有细胞核、靠分裂繁殖的单细胞生物
senses.example: Bacteria are far older than animals and live almost everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌比动物古老得多，几乎无处不在。
senses.why: The word is a Latin plural, so it is grammatically plural: bacteria are, not bacteria is. The singular bacterium survives in scientific writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拉丁复数，因此语法上是复数：说 bacteria are，而不是 bacteria is。单数 bacterium 仍存活于科学写作中。

senses.title: Gut bacteria
senses.titleCN: 肠道细菌：定居在消化道中的菌群
senses.definition: the community of bacteria that lives in the intestine and helps digest food, make vitamins and train the immune system
senses.definitionCN: 生活在肠道、帮助消化、合成维生素并训练免疫系统的细菌群
senses.example: Bacteria in the gut help break down food that the body cannot digest alone.
senses.exampleCN: 肠道里的细菌帮助分解身体无法独自消化的食物。
senses.why: The word is often used of a community rather than of individual cells, because what matters in a body is the population and what it does together.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常指一个群落而非单个细胞，因为在身体里真正要紧的是这个群体及它们共同做的事。

senses.title: Pathogenic bacteria
senses.titleCN: 致病细菌：引起感染的那一部分
senses.definition: those bacteria able to invade tissue and cause disease, as opposed to the harmless majority
senses.definitionCN: 能侵入组织并引起疾病的细菌，与无害的大多数相对
senses.example: Only a small fraction of bacteria cause disease in humans.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一小部分细菌会使人类致病。
senses.why: Public anxiety treats all bacteria as germs, but the technical use keeps the distinction, and the modifier pathogenic marks the exception.
senses.whyCN: 公众的焦虑把一切细菌都当成病原，但技术用法保留区分，并用 pathogenic 这一修饰语标出例外。

senses.title: Beneficial bacteria
senses.titleCN: 有益细菌：用于发酵、益生菌与生物防治
senses.definition: bacteria used for their helpful effects, in food cultures, probiotics or biological control
senses.definitionCN: 因其有益作用而被使用的细菌，如食品发酵菌、益生菌或生物防治菌
senses.example: Beneficial bacteria turn milk into yoghurt overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 有益细菌在一夜之间把牛奶变成酸奶。
senses.why: Fermentation is ancient practice, and modern language describes it with the same noun, showing that the category is neutral and only the modifier judges it.
senses.whyCN: 发酵是古老实践，现代语言用同一个名词描述它，说明这个类别本身是中性的，只是修饰语在作判断。

senses.title: Soil bacteria
senses.titleCN: 土壤细菌：参与分解与养分循环
senses.definition: bacteria living in soil that break down organic matter and recycle nitrogen and other nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 生活在土壤中、分解有机物并循环氮等养分的细菌
senses.example: Soil bacteria release nitrogen that plants can use.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤细菌释放出植物可利用的氮。
senses.why: The same organisms that decay leaves also feed crops, so ecology uses the word for the whole functional group rather than for a species.
senses.whyCN: 分解落叶的正是为作物提供养分的那批生物，因此生态学用这个词指整个功能群，而非某个物种。

senses.title: Bacteria in food
senses.titleCN: 食品中的细菌：发酵菌与腐败菌
senses.definition: bacteria present in food, whether useful cultures that preserve or flavour it or spoilage organisms that ruin it
senses.definitionCN: 食品中的细菌，既包括保存或增味的发酵菌，也包括使食物变质的腐败菌
senses.example: The cheese depends on bacteria that ripen it from the inside.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪依赖从内部使其熟成的细菌。
senses.why: Food science needs one word for both the culture and the contaminant, and the outcome, not the organism, decides which label is used.
senses.whyCN: 食品科学需要一个词同时涵盖发酵菌与污染物，而决定用哪个标签的是结果，而非生物本身。

senses.title: Laboratory model
senses.titleCN: 实验模型细菌：研究遗传与代谢的工具
senses.definition: bacteria used as model organisms in research, because they grow fast and are easy to manipulate genetically
senses.definitionCN: 因生长快、易于遗传操作而在研究中被用作模式生物的细菌
senses.example: Bacteria such as E. coli are the workhorses of molecular biology.
senses.exampleCN: 大肠杆菌这类细菌是分子生物学的主力。
senses.why: A short generation time turns a cell into an experimental tool, and the plural noun names the whole set of standard organisms.
senses.whyCN: 很短的世代时间把细胞变成实验工具，复数名词便指整套标准模式生物。

senses.title: The taxonomic group
senses.titleCN: 细菌界：分类学上的一个域或界
senses.definition: in taxonomy, the large group Bacteria, one of the highest divisions of life, distinct from archaea and eukaryotes
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中的细菌大群，是生命最高层级划分之一，与古菌和真核生物并列
senses.example: Bacteria form one of the three domains of life.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌构成生命的三大域之一。
senses.why: When the word is capitalised and used as a taxon, it stops meaning 'some germs' and starts naming an entire branch of the tree of life.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词首字母大写并作为分类单元使用时，它不再指「某些病菌」，而是命名生命之树的一整支。

intro.en: Bacteria is the plural of Latin bacterium, a modern scientific Latin word from Greek baktērion 'small staff', because the first ones seen were rod-shaped. It has been treated as a plural noun in English since the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: bacteria 是拉丁 bacterium 的复数，后者是现代科学拉丁词，来自希腊 baktērion「小棒」，因为最早被看见的细菌是杆状的。19 世纪以来英语一直把它当复数名词用。

items.en: Baktron meant a stick or staff; the diminutive baktērion meant a small rod, and had nothing to do with disease.
items.cn: baktron 指棍棒；小称 baktērion 意为小棒，与疾病毫无关系。

items.en: Scientific Latin formed bacterium as a singular noun for a rod-shaped microbe, with the plural bacteria following Latin first-declension neuter patterns.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语造出 bacterium，作为杆状微生物的单数名词，复数 bacteria 依拉丁第一变格中性名词的模式构成。

items.en: The German naturalist Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg used Bacterium as a genus name for rod-shaped microbes in the late 1820s, and the term spread through microscopy.
items.cn: 德国博物学家克里斯蒂安·戈特弗里德·埃伦伯格在 1820 年代后期把 Bacterium 用作杆状微生物的属名，这个词随显微镜研究传播开来。

items.en: In the later nineteenth century bacteria became the central object of germ theory, and the plural became the ordinary English word for the whole class.
items.cn: 19 世纪后期细菌成为病菌学说的核心对象，复数形式成为指整类的日常英语词。

items.en: Staining and culture methods made bacteria countable and classifiable, and the word entered medicine, food science and agriculture.
items.cn: 染色与培养方法使细菌变得可计数、可分类，这个词进入医学、食品科学与农业。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact year of Ehrenberg's genus name is variously given as 1828 or the early 1830s, and the first English use of bacteria as a common noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：埃伦伯格属名的确切年份有 1828 年与 1830 年代初两种说法，bacteria 作为普通名词的英语首见年代亦无精确记载。

note.en: The first group holds the singular and the look-alike terms built on the same stem; the second holds the other microbes and the words for what bacteria do.
note.cn: 第一组是单数形式与同词干的形近词；第二组是其他微生物，以及描述细菌作用的名词。

entries.definition: One bacterial cell; bacteria is its plural, so 'a bacteria' is a mistake in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 单个细菌细胞；bacteria 是其复数，因此正式写作中「a bacteria」是错误。

entries.definition: Relating to bacteria, as in bacterial infection; it describes the cause, not the organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 与细菌有关，如细菌感染；它描述病因，而非生物本身。

entries.definition: The study of bacteria; it is a science, while bacteria are its objects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究细菌的学科；它是一门科学，而细菌是它的研究对象。

entries.definition: A substance that kills bacteria; the -cide element means 'killing'.
entries.definitionCN: 杀灭细菌的物质；-cide 成分意为「杀」。

entries.definition: An infectious agent that reproduces only inside a host cell and has no independent metabolism; much smaller than bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 只能在宿主细胞内复制、没有独立代谢的感染因子；比细菌小得多。

entries.definition: Single-celled organisms without a nucleus but chemically distinct from bacteria; they often live in extreme environments.
entries.definitionCN: 无细胞核、但生化上与细菌不同的单细胞生物，常生活在极端环境。

entries.definition: Any microscopic organism, including bacteria, archaea, fungi and protozoa.
entries.definitionCN: 任何微小生物，包括细菌、古菌、真菌与原虫。

entries.definition: A preparation of live beneficial bacteria taken for health; it names a product, not the organisms' taxonomy.
entries.definitionCN: 为健康而摄入的活性有益菌制品；它命名产品，而非生物分类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek baktron 'staff' gives baktērion 'small rod', the shape of the first ones seen.
normal.cn: 希腊 baktron「棍」生 baktērion「小棒」，正是最早被看见的细菌形状。

normal.en: bacteria is plural: bacteria are, one bacterium; keep the pair straight.
normal.cn: bacteria 是复数：说 bacteria are、单数用 bacterium；把这一对记清。

normal.en: The family runs bacterium, bacteria, bacterial, bacteriology, bactericide.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 bacterium、bacteria、bacterial、bacteriology、bactericide。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name habitats: gut bacteria, soil bacteria, beneficial bacteria.
normal.cn: 固定搭配命名栖息地：肠道细菌、土壤细菌、有益细菌。

normal.en: Do not treat bacteria and viruses as the same: one is a cell, the other needs a cell.
normal.cn: 不要把细菌与病毒混为一谈：一个是细胞，另一个需要细胞才能复制。

abstract.en: Picture a field of tiny rods under a lens, none of them with a nucleus.
abstract.cn: 想象镜头下的一片小棒，没有一个带细胞核。

abstract.en: Picture a city of invisible workers recycling everything that falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一座看不见的工人之城，把落下的东西全部回收。

abstract.en: Picture a single cell splitting into two, then four, within an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞在一小时内分成两个，再分成四个。

examples.en: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses.
examples.cn: 抗生素杀细菌，但对病毒无效。

examples.en: Some bacteria can survive boiling and dry heat.
examples.cn: 有些细菌能耐受煮沸与干热。

examples.en: The number of bacteria in a gram of soil runs into the millions.
examples.cn: 一克土壤中的细菌数量可达数百万。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bacterium 的单数 → bacteria 复数」——记住 are 配 bacteria，is 配 bacterium → bacteria 细菌

root: 希腊 baktron「棍棒」→ 小称 baktērion「小棒」→ 科学拉丁 bacterium（单数）→ 英语 bacteria（复数，19 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one class of cells: the grammatical plural, the gut community, the disease-causing minority, the useful cultures, soil recyclers, food organisms, laboratory models, and finally the taxonomic domain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一类细胞展开：语法上的复数、肠道菌群、致病的少数、有用的发酵菌、土壤分解者、食品中的菌、实验室模式生物，最后是分类学上的域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field of tiny rod-shaped cells with no nucleus, dividing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片没有细胞核的微小杆状细胞，正在分裂。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a Latin plural used as a plural English noun.
branches.cn: 语法：作为英语复数名词使用的拉丁复数。

branches.en: INSIDE THE BODY: the community that helps, and the minority that harms.
branches.cn: 身体之内：帮助消化的群落，以及造成伤害的少数。

branches.en: USEFUL WORK: fermentation and probiotics turn the same class into tools and products.
branches.cn: 有益工作：发酵与益生菌把同一类细胞变成工具与产品。

branches.en: OUTSIDE: soil bacteria drive the nutrient cycle.
branches.cn: 身体之外：土壤细菌驱动养分循环。

branches.en: MODEL AND TREE: the lab uses a few species, while taxonomy names the whole branch.
branches.cn: 模型与谱系：实验室只用少数物种，分类学则命名整支。

intro.en: Bacteria is a plural Latin form in -a; the stem bacter- builds bacterial, bacteriology and bactericide, with -ium for the singular.
intro.cn: bacteria 是以 -a 结尾的拉丁复数；词干 bacter- 造出 bacterial、bacteriology、bactericide，单数则用 -ium。

latinIntro.en: Modern Latin bacterium comes from Greek baktērion; the Greek diminutive suffix -ion is the source of the Latin -ium, which then yields the plural -ia and English -a.
latinIntro.cn: 现代拉丁 bacterium 来自希腊 baktērion；希腊小称后缀 -ion 是拉丁 -ium 的来源，后者再产生复数 -ia 与英语 -a。

items.example: Bacteria are classified by shape and staining.
items.exampleCN: 细菌按形状与染色分类。

items.example: A single bacterium can start a colony.
items.exampleCN: 一个细菌就能起始一个菌落。

items.example: The infection was bacterial, not viral.
items.exampleCN: 这是细菌感染，而非病毒感染。
细菌学家鉴定了该菌株。

items.example: The drug is bactericidal rather than bacteriostatic.
items.exampleCN: 这种药是杀菌性的，而非抑菌性的。
噬菌体在抗生素之前就已被使用。

latinEntries.structure: Modern Latin, from Greek baktērion (n., second declension)

latinEntries.meaningCN: 小棒（拉丁语，与希腊 baktērion 语义对应的另一词）

definition_zh: 寄生物；寄生虫；靠他人养活的人
definition_en: an organism that lives on or in another organism and feeds at its expense, or a person who lives at others' expense
core_image: 一条细长的蠕虫钩在宿主肠壁上，宿主的血流在旁边经过
scene: 这里指「寄生物」。 The parasite feeds on the host's blood without killing it at once.
sceneCN: 这里 parasite 是「寄生物」（第 1 个义项：靠宿主供养的生物）；句意：这种寄生物吸食宿主的血，却不立即杀死宿主。图中可辨识物件：钩在肠壁上的蠕虫、流经的血管、宿主的身体轮廓。

pos.zh: 寄生物；寄生虫（可数名词，复数 parasites）；也指靠他人供养的人（贬义）

derivatives.zh: 超寄生物（寄生于寄生物的生物）

senses.title: The Biological Parasite
senses.titleCN: 寄生物：靠宿主供养的另一种生物
senses.definition: an organism that lives on or in a host and obtains nutrients from it
senses.definitionCN: 生活在宿主体表或体内、从宿主获取养分的生物
senses.example: The parasite draws nutrients from the host without contributing any.
senses.exampleCN: 这种寄生物从宿主身上吸取养分，却没有任何贡献。
senses.why: Greek parasitos meant 'one who eats at another's table'. Biology kept the table metaphor: the parasite takes food from a host that pays for it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 parasitos 意为「在别人餐桌上吃饭的人」；生物学保留了这个餐桌隐喻：寄生物从付账的宿主那里取食。

senses.title: A Human Parasite
senses.titleCN: 人体寄生虫：感染人的蠕虫与原虫
senses.definition: a parasite that infects human beings, such as a tapeworm or a protozoan
senses.definitionCN: 感染人类的寄生物，如绦虫或原虫
senses.example: The child was treated for an intestinal parasite.
senses.exampleCN: 这个孩子因肠道寄生虫接受了治疗。
senses.why: In medicine the word usually names a worm or a protozoan, not a bacterium or a virus. The host is specified as human, and the sense becomes a clinical category.
senses.whyCN: 在医学中这个词通常指蠕虫或原虫，而不是细菌或病毒；宿主被限定为人类，该义项成为一个临床类别。

senses.title: A Plant Parasite
senses.titleCN: 植物寄生物：附着在其他植物上
senses.definition: a plant that lives on another plant and takes water or nutrients from it
senses.definitionCN: 附着在另一种植物上、从中获取水分或养分的植物
senses.example: Mistletoe is a plant parasite that draws water from its tree.
senses.exampleCN: 槲寄生是一种植物寄生物，从树上吸取水分。
senses.why: Plants can parasitise too. The technical sense extends the table metaphor to a tree as host, and the feeding organ replaces the gut.
senses.whyCN: 植物也会寄生；这一技术义把餐桌隐喻扩展到树木作宿主，吸器取代了肠道。

senses.title: A Social Parasite
senses.titleCN: 社会寄生虫：靠他人生活的人
senses.definition: a person who lives at the expense of others without contributing
senses.definitionCN: 靠他人供养而自己不付出的人
senses.example: He called his brother-in-law a parasite for never paying rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不付房租的姐夫为寄生虫。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the Greek word described a flatterer who ate at rich tables. The modern insult keeps the same image, now with moral disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：希腊词描述的是在富人餐桌上蹭饭的奉承者；现代骂人话保留了同一画面，只是加了道德谴责。

senses.title: A Brood Parasite
senses.titleCN: 巢寄生鸟：让别人代养幼鸟
senses.definition: a bird that lays its eggs in another species' nest
senses.definitionCN: 把蛋产在另一种鸟巢中、由对方代养的鸟
senses.example: The brood parasite's chick pushed the host's eggs out of the nest.
senses.exampleCN: 这只巢寄生鸟的雏鸟把宿主的蛋挤出了巢。
senses.why: Here the host is a parent, not a body. The sense shows that parasitism is about transferred cost, not necessarily about feeding on tissue.
senses.whyCN: 这里的宿主是亲鸟，而不是身体；这个义项说明寄生的本质是成本转移，而不一定是取食组织。

senses.title: Obligate and Facultative
senses.titleCN: 专性与兼性：依赖程度的分型
senses.definition: a parasite classified by whether it cannot survive without a host
senses.definitionCN: 按是否离开宿主便无法生存而划分的寄生物类型
senses.example: An obligate parasite dies when separated from its host.
senses.exampleCN: 专性寄生物一旦离开宿主就会死亡。
senses.why: The word can carry a subtype label. Obligate means the host is a necessity; facultative means the parasite can also live freely. The distinction measures dependence, the core of S1.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以带亚型标签：专性表示宿主是必需品，兼性表示它也能自由生活；这一区分衡量的正是第 1 个义项的核心——依赖程度。

senses.title: Parasite Load
senses.titleCN: 寄生虫负荷：体内寄生物的数量
senses.definition: the number of parasites carried by one host
senses.definitionCN: 一个宿主身上携带的寄生物数量
senses.example: A high parasite load weakened the herd.
senses.exampleCN: 较高的寄生虫负荷削弱了兽群。
senses.why: Load makes the parasite countable. The phrase shifts from the organism to the burden it places on a host, which is the quantity clinicians and ecologists actually measure.
senses.whyCN: 「负荷」使寄生物变得可计数；这个短语从生物体转向它加在宿主身上的负担，而这一数量才是临床医生与生态学家真正测量的东西。

senses.title: A Parasite on the Economy
senses.titleCN: 经济寄生虫：依附于系统获利
senses.definition: an entity or activity that drains a system without producing value
senses.definitionCN: 只消耗系统而不创造价值的实体或活动
senses.example: The report described the shell companies as parasites on the tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把那些空壳公司称为税收系统的寄生虫。
senses.why: The metaphor moves from a person to an institution: something attaches to a system and takes from it. It differs from S4 by scale and by the abstraction of the host.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻从个人移到机构：某物附着在系统上并从中索取；它与第 4 个义项的区别在于尺度，以及宿主被抽象化。

intro.en: Parasite came from a Greek word for a dinner guest who paid nothing. Science adopted it in the seventeenth century for a creature that lives at a host's expense, and the insult travelled alongside the biology.
intro.cn: parasite 来自一个希腊词，指不付钱的白食客人。科学在十七世纪采用它，指靠宿主供养的生物，而骂人的用法一直与生物学用法并行。

items.en: Greek parasitos meant 'one who lives at another's expense, person who eats at the table of another', especially a flatterer who earned his dinner by praise. It was a noun use of an adjective meaning 'feeding beside'.
items.cn: 希腊语 parasitos 意为「靠他人供养的人、在别人餐桌上吃饭的人」，尤指靠奉承换取晚餐的人；它是由意为「在旁边取食」的形容词转成的名词。

items.en: The first element is para- 'beside'. The second is sitos 'grain, bread, food', a word of unknown origin. It also appears in syssitos 'table companion'. Sitos is often explained as a loanword or substrate word; Beekes suggests a link to a root meaning 'to strike', but this is disputed, so the origin of the second element is uncertain.
items.cn: 第一个成分是 para-「在旁边」，第二个是 sitos「谷物、面包、食物」，其来源不确定。它也出现在 syssitos「同桌吃饭的人」中。sitos 常被解释为借词或底层词；Beekes 提出可能与意为「击打」的词根有关，但这仍有争议，因此第二成分的来源不确定。

items.en: English borrowed parasite in the 1530s for a hanger-on or toady, a social meaning that came straight from Greek comedy. The scientific sense appears in the 1640s.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪三十年代借入 parasite，指攀附者或马屁精，这一社会义直接来自希腊喜剧；科学义则在十七世纪四十年代出现。

items.en: The sense 'animal or plant that lives on or in and at the expense of another' is recorded from the 1640s, implied in parasitical. It kept the Greek picture of eating at someone else's table.
items.cn: 「生活在他者体表或体内、靠他者供养的动物或植物」这一义项记录于十七世纪四十年代，在 parasitical 中已有体现；它保留了希腊语「在别人桌上吃饭」的画面。

items.en: Parasitic is recorded from the 1620s, parasitism from the 1610s, and the biological senses of both followed in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The words existed first as social labels.
items.cn: parasitic 记录于十七世纪二十年代，parasitism 记录于十七世纪十年代，两者的生物学义则分别到十八、十九世纪才出现；这些词最初都是社会标签。

items.en: Parasitology grew as a medical and veterinary field once the life cycles of worms and protozoa were worked out. The word now spans everything from malaria to brood parasitism in birds.
items.cn: 当蠕虫与原虫的生活史被弄清之后，寄生虫学作为医学与兽医学领域发展起来；这个词现在涵盖从疟疾到鸟类巢寄生的广泛现象。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and abstract noun. The second group holds ecological roles and everyday insults that are often confused with parasite.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词与其形容词、抽象名词；第二组是常与 parasite 混淆的生态角色与日常贬义词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'living as a parasite'. It describes the mode of life, not the organism itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以寄生方式生活的」形容词；描述生活方式，而不是生物体本身。

entries.definition: The relationship between parasite and host. It names the arrangement, while parasite names one partner.
entries.definitionCN: 寄生物与宿主之间的关系；它命名这种安排，而 parasite 命名其中一方。

entries.definition: To live on or in a host as a parasite. It is the action verb, not a noun for the actor.
entries.definitionCN: 指以寄生物方式生活在宿主身上或体内；它是动作动词，不是施动者的名词。

entries.definition: Any agent that causes disease. A parasite may be a pathogen, but many parasites cause little or no disease, and bacteria are pathogens without being parasites.
entries.definitionCN: 任何引起疾病的因子；寄生物可能是病原，但许多寄生物几乎不致病，而细菌可以是病原却不是寄生物。

entries.definition: An organism living in close association with another. The term is neutral, while parasite names a cost to the host.
entries.definitionCN: 与其他生物密切共同生活的生物；这个术语是中性的，而 parasite 命名的是宿主付出的代价。

entries.tag: noun adjective one who shares a ta
entries.definition: An organism that lives with a host and takes food from it without harming it. It is literally 'at the same table', a milder version of parasite.
entries.definitionCN: 与宿主共同生活、从其处取食却不伤害它的生物；字面意为「同桌吃饭」，是 parasite 的温和版本。

entries.definition: An informal word for a person who takes without paying. It is the everyday equivalent of the social sense, with less bite than parasite.
entries.definitionCN: 指只索取不付钱的人的非正式词；它是社会义项的日常对应词，语气比 parasite 稍轻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: para- 'beside' + sitos 'food': one who eats beside another's table, and pays nothing.
normal.cn: para-「在旁边」+ sitos「食物」：在别人餐桌旁吃饭而不付钱的人。

normal.en: The insult came first in English, in the 1530s; the biological sense followed in the 1640s.
normal.cn: 英语里骂人的用法先出现，在十六世纪三十年代；生物学义到十七世纪四十年代才跟上。

normal.en: The family runs parasite, parasites, parasitic, parasitism, parasitize, parasitology and parasitologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 parasite、parasites、parasitic、parasitism、parasitize、parasitology、parasitologist。

normal.en: Obligate means it cannot leave the host; facultative means it can.
normal.cn: 专性表示离不开宿主，兼性表示可以离开。

normal.en: A parasite takes; a commensal shares; a mutualist gives back.
normal.cn: 寄生物索取，共栖者同吃，互利者回报。

abstract.en: Picture a guest who arrives for dinner and never leaves, and never brings anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一位来吃晚饭的客人，从此不走，也从不带任何东西。

abstract.en: Picture a hook sunk into a wall that draws water from the other side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钩子扎进墙里，从另一边抽水。

abstract.en: Picture a company with no product, only a claim on the public purse.
abstract.cn: 想象一家没有产品、只对公共财政伸手的公司。

examples.en: The parasite completes its life cycle inside two different hosts.
examples.cn: 这种寄生物在两个不同的宿主体内完成生活史。

examples.en: Researchers measured the parasite load in each fish.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了每条鱼的寄生虫负荷。

examples.en: He was a parasite on his friends' generosity for years.
examples.cn: 多年来他一直靠朋友们的慷慨过活，是个寄生虫。

dict_mnemonic.text: para-（在旁边）+ sitos（食物）→ 在旁边吃别人的饭 → parasite 寄生物；靠他人供养的人

root: 希腊 para-「在旁边」+ sitos「谷物、食物」（来源不明，可能为借词或底层词）→ parasitos「在别人餐桌上吃饭的人」→ 拉丁 parasitus → 法语 parasite → 英语 parasite（1530s 指攀附者；1640s 出现生物学义）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the table metaphor outward: a biological freeloader, a human infection, a plant, a social hanger-on, a nest usurper, a dependence type, a measured burden and an institution draining a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着餐桌隐喻向外扩展：生物学白食者、人体感染、植物、社会攀附者、占巢者、依赖类型、可测量的负担，以及吸干系统的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small body attached to a larger one, drawing food through a hook.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小身体附着在更大的身体上，通过钩子抽取食物。

branches.en: DEFINITION: the biological core, feeding at a host's expense.
branches.cn: 定义：生物学核心，靠宿主付账取食。

branches.en: HOST KINDS: the host can be a human body or a plant, and the feeding organ changes with it.
branches.cn: 宿主种类：宿主可以是人体或植物，取食器官也随之改变。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND NEST COST: the cost can be rent-free living or childcare, not only food.
branches.cn: 社会与巢中的代价：代价可以是白住或代养，而不只是食物。

branches.en: DEGREE AND MEASURE: dependence can be obligate or facultative, and the burden can be counted as a load.
branches.cn: 程度与测量：依赖可以是专性或兼性，负担可以按负荷计数。

branches.en: ABSTRACT HOST: the metaphor can attach a company or an activity to an economy.
branches.cn: 抽象宿主：这个隐喻可以把一家公司或一项活动附着到经济体上。

intro.en: Parasite is a Greek compound borrowed through Latin and French. Its family grows with Greek and Latin suffixes that turn the noun into an adjective, a relationship, a verb and a science.
intro.cn: parasite 是经拉丁语与法语借入的希腊复合词；它的词族靠希腊与拉丁后缀生长，把名词变成形容词、关系名词、动词与学科名。

latinIntro.en: Latin parasitus meant 'toady, sponger', a direct borrowing from Greek parasitos. The suffix -ic, -ism and -ize were added in English and French rather than in classical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 parasitus 意为「马屁精、白食者」，直接借自希腊 parasitos；后缀 -ic、-ism 与 -ize 是在英语与法语中加上的，而非古典拉丁语。

definition_en: a sign that shows an illness or a deeper problem
core_image: 体温计上的水银升到红色刻度，医生记下这笔
scene: 发烧是感染的常见症状。 Fever is a common symptom of infection.
sceneCN: 这里 symptom 是「症状」（第 1 个义项）；句意：发烧是感染的常见症状。

senses.title: A sign of illness
senses.definition: a change in the body that shows a disease
senses.definitionCN: 显示疾病的身体变化
senses.example: Fever is a common symptom of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧是感染的常见症状。
senses.why: The Greek word meant a chance happening that falls together with something else.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为与某事同时发生的偶然现象。

senses.title: A sign of a wider problem
senses.definition: a sign that something else is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 表明其他方面出了问题的迹象
senses.example: Rising debt is a symptom of deeper trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 债务上升是更深层问题的征兆。
senses.why: If a bodily sign can point to a disease, any sign can point to a hidden cause.
senses.whyCN: 身体迹象可以指向疾病，任何迹象也就能指向隐藏的根源。

intro.en: Symptom comes from Greek symptoma, something that falls together.
intro.cn: symptom 源自希腊语 symptoma，意为同时发生之事。

items.en: Symptoma meant a chance event falling with another.
items.cn: symptoma 意为与另一事同时发生的偶然事件。

items.en: Piptein meant to fall.
items.cn: piptein 意为落下。

items.en: Symptoma became a medical term for a sign of disease.
items.cn: symptoma 成为指疾病迹象的医学术语。

items.en: French symptome carried the medical sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 symptome 把医学含义带入英语。

items.en: Symptom widened to signs of any deeper problem.
items.cn: symptom 扩展到任何深层问题的迹象。

note.en: Symptom is compared with look-alike words and with other signs.
note.cn: 把 symptom 与形近词以及其他表示迹象的词作比较。

abstract.en: Every symptom is a small arrow pointing inward.

definition_en: moving or pointing toward a lower place, level, or amount
core_image: 一条箭头贴着纸面向下压出的斜线
scene: 山道在脚下突然折低，扶手顺着坡度一路向下延伸。 The path takes a downward turn just past the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 downward 是「向下的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是小路刚过大门就转为向下。

derivatives.zh: 由 downward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向下地」，多见于英式英语
由 downward 加 -ly 构成，义为「向下地」，书面语中偶见

senses.title: Moving toward a lower place
senses.definition: going or pointing from a higher position to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 从较高位置朝较低位置去或指向低处
senses.example: A downward path leads to the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 一条向下的小路通向海滩。
senses.why: The suffix -ward means turned in a direction, so downward is simply down plus a sense of facing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ward 表示「朝某个方向转过去」，所以 downward 就是 down 加上「面朝」的意思。

senses.title: Decreasing in amount or value
senses.definition: showing a fall in numbers, prices, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 显示数量、价格或质量在下跌
senses.example: The report notes a downward trend in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出销量呈下降趋势。
senses.why: Since falling numbers move toward the ground on a chart, the direction word also describes any decline.
senses.whyCN: 在图表上，数字下跌就是朝地面方向走，所以这个方向词也用来描述任何下滑。

senses.title: In a downward direction
senses.definition: used as an adverb meaning toward a lower position, mainly in American English
senses.definitionCN: 作副词表示朝较低位置，主要用于美式英语
senses.example: He adjusted the mirror downward.
senses.exampleCN: 他把镜子朝下调整。
senses.why: English often uses one -ward form for both adjective and adverb, so the same word can modify a verb.
senses.whyCN: 英语里 -ward 形式常兼作形容词与副词，所以同一个词也能修饰动词。

intro.en: Downward is down plus the Old English suffix -weard, meaning turned toward.
intro.cn: downward 是 down 加上古英语后缀 -weard（朝……转）构成的。

items.en: Dun meant hill, and its dative dune gave the direction word down.
items.cn: 古英语 dun 意为「山丘」，其与格 dune 产生了方向词 down。

items.en: Weard meant turned toward and built words such as hameweard, homeward.
items.cn: weard 意为「朝向」，构成 hameweard（向家）一类词。

items.en: The two elements were combined to describe a slope facing downward; the exact early spelling varies.
items.cn: 两个成分被组合起来描述朝下的坡面；早期拼写形式并不统一。

items.en: The form settled as downward and kept both the adverbial and the descriptive use.
items.cn: 形式固定为 downward，副词与修饰用法并存。

items.en: British usage prefers downwards for the adverb, while American usage often keeps downward for both.
items.cn: 英式英语的副词多用 downwards，美式英语则常两种词性都用 downward。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ward build; the near-meaning group compares three words for falling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ward 构词；近义组比较三个表示「下降」的词。

entries.definition: The adverbial form, common in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向下地」，英式英语中更常见。

entries.definition: Moving or pointing toward a higher place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「向上的」，与 downward 方向相反。

entries.definition: Toward home; built with the same old suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「回家的」，用的是同一个古老后缀。

entries.definition: Becoming smaller or weaker over time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的、衰退的」，强调随时间变弱。

entries.definition: Going down in level or amount; plainer than downward.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的」，比 downward 更口语。

entries.definition: Moving from a higher to a lower point, often in a formal or technical tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「下降的」，语体偏正式或技术性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the -ward suffix and the difference between the adjective and the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子围绕 -ward 后缀，以及形容词与副词的分工展开。

normal.en: -Ward means turned toward, so downward is simply facing the ground.
normal.cn: -ward 意为「朝向」，所以 downward 就是「面朝地面」。

normal.en: A downward trend draws a line that slides toward the bottom of the chart.
normal.cn: downward trend 画出的是一条滑向图表底部的线。

normal.en: British speakers add -s for the adverb, giving downwards.
normal.cn: 英式英语给副词加 -s，写成 downwards。

normal.en: Upward is the exact mirror image, made with up instead of down.
normal.cn: upward 是它精确的镜像，只把 down 换成 up。

normal.en: Homeward proves the suffix is still productive in modern English.
normal.cn: homeward 证明这个后缀在现代英语里仍能造词。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow pasted flat on a page pointing at the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚箭头贴在纸面上直指地面。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase drawn as a single line sliding down to the right.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯被画成一条向右下滑的线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a lift button with a downward triangle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按下带向下三角的电梯按钮。

examples.en: The downward slope was slippery after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后那段下坡很滑。

examples.en: Economists warn of downward pressure on wages.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告工资面临下行压力。

examples.en: She tilted the lamp downward to read the map.
examples.cn: 她把灯往下压，好看清地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: down 是「向下」，-ward 是「朝……方向」，合起来就是「朝下的」，也可直接当副词用。

root: 由 down（向下）加古英语后缀 -weard（朝向）构成，同族词还有 homeward、upward 等。down 本身来自古英语 dun（山丘）的与格 dune；-weard 在日耳曼语中表示「转向某方向」。

sensesIntro.en: The suffix adds direction to the old word down, then the direction extends from space to numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 后缀给古老的 down 加上了方向，这个方向又从空间延伸到数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow pressed flat against the page, pointing at the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚贴在纸面上、直指地面的箭头。

branches.en: SPACE: the basic use describes anything pointing to a lower place.
branches.cn: 空间线：基本用法描述任何指向低处的事物，即第一个义项。

branches.en: NUMBERS: plotted values fall toward the bottom, so the word labels a decline.
branches.cn: 数字线：画在图上的数值朝底部落，于是这个词标注下降，即第二个义项。

branches.en: ACTION: the same form can modify a verb in American usage.
branches.cn: 动作线：在美式用法里，同一形式可以修饰动词，即第三个义项。

branches.en: A downward path and moving downward describe the same motion from two angles.
branches.cn: 向下的路与向下移动，是从两个角度描述同一个动作。

branches.en: A downward trend is what you see when prices keep moving downward.
branches.cn: 当价格持续向下移动时，你看到的就是下降趋势。

intro.en: Downward is a native English build of a direction word and a suffix of facing.
intro.cn: downward 是英语本族构词：一个方向词加一个表示「朝向」的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element; the suffix -weard is shared across the Germanic languages.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；后缀 -weard 在日耳曼诸语言中通用。

items.exampleCN: down 是 downward 的基础。
