definition_zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；使成熟；成熟；到期
definition_en: fully grown or fully developed, especially in fruit, wine, or a person; showing adult judgment; as a verb, to become fully developed or to reach the date when a financial product must be paid
core_image: 枝头的果子由青转红：酸涩退去，甜味与重量一起到位，才到了可以摘下的那一刻
scene: 果园里，农人捏了捏枝头的桃子。 The peach gave slightly under his thumb, and only when it was mature did he cut it down and put it in the basket.
sceneCN: 这里 mature 是「果实成熟」（第 1 个义项：水果、作物达到可食用的成熟状态）；句意：桃子在他拇指下微微软了，只有确认它成熟了，他才摘下来放进筐里。图中可辨识物件：桃树枝、成熟的桃子、农人的手、果筐；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 成熟的；成年的；深思熟虑的；到期的

senses.title: Fruit or wine: ripe and ready
senses.titleCN: 果实或酒：熟到可以用了
senses.definition: of fruit, grain, or wine, fully ripened and ready to be eaten, harvested, or drunk
senses.definitionCN: 指水果、谷物或酒已完全成熟，可以食用、收割或饮用
senses.example: The peaches are mature enough to pick today.
senses.exampleCN: 这些桃子今天已经熟到可以摘了。
senses.why: The adjective is first recorded in the mid-15c. of fruits, meaning 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development'. The image is biological: growth has finished, and the fruit has reached the point it was growing toward.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义在 15 世纪中期首次记录，用于水果，意为“成熟的、在自然生长或发育上已完成的”。画面是生物性的：生长已经结束，果实到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。

senses.title: A person fully grown in body and mind
senses.definition: of a person, having fully developed powers of body and mind; adult
senses.definitionCN: 指人在身体与心智能力上已充分发育；成年的
senses.example: The study compares mature adults with teenagers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把成年人与青少年作比较。
senses.why: Of persons, the sense 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The biological image is transferred from fruit to people: development has reached its intended end, though growth in learning may continue.
senses.whyCN: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”的义项记录于约 1600 年。生物意象从果实移到了人：发育已达到预定的终点，尽管学识上的成长仍可继续。

senses.title: Adult judgment: behaving with maturity
senses.titleCN: 成年人的判断力：表现得成熟
senses.definition: showing the emotional calm and responsibility expected of an adult, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 在困难处境中表现出成年人应有的情绪稳定与责任感
senses.example: She gave a mature answer instead of blaming someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有责怪别人，而是给出了一个成熟的回答。
senses.why: This is the evaluative branch: mature no longer describes the body but the response. The word praises someone for having reached the emotional end-point that adulthood is supposed to bring.
senses.whyCN: 这是评价性的分支：mature 描述的不再是身体，而是反应方式。这个词在称赞一个人达到了成年本应带来的情绪终点。

senses.title: A well-considered plan or judgment
senses.titleCN: 经过充分考虑的计划或判断
senses.definition: of a plan, idea, or judgment, careful, thorough, and reached after long thought
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、想法或判断审慎、周全，并经过长时间思考才形成
senses.example: After months of review, they submitted a mature proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数月审议，他们提交了一份成熟的方案。
senses.why: The same mid-15c. entry that named ripe fruit also named 'careful, well-considered, thorough' deliberations. An idea, like fruit, needs time before it is ready; rushing it gives a green, sour result.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中期记录“成熟果实”的同一条目，也记录了“审慎、周全、彻底”的思考。一个想法和果实一样，需要时间才能就绪；催熟只会得到青涩的结果。

senses.title: To ripen: make or become mature
senses.definition: to bring something to full ripeness, or to come to a state of ripeness
senses.definitionCN: 使某物完全成熟，或进入成熟状态
senses.example: The cheese is left to mature for eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这种奶酪要放置十八个月让它成熟。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1400 as 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen'. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' is from the 1650s. The medical origin is literal: a swelling also comes to a head in its own time.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1400 年出现，意为“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟”。“自己变得成熟”的不及物义来自 17 世纪 50 年代。医学来源是字面的：肿胀也会在自己的时间里“长熟”。

senses.title: A market, product, or artist developing fully
senses.titleCN: 市场、产品或艺术家发展至完善
senses.definition: of an industry, product, style, or career, to develop over time into a settled and fully formed state
senses.definitionCN: 指行业、产品、风格或事业随时间发展，进入稳定而完整的状态
senses.example: The market matured quickly once the standards were agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 标准一旦达成一致，这个市场很快就成熟了。
senses.why: Growth in business follows the same curve as growth in a plant: an early unstable phase, then a settled phase. Calling a market mature means it has stopped expanding wildly and has found its shape.
senses.whyCN: 商业上的成长与植物的成长走同一条曲线：先是早期不稳定阶段，然后是稳定阶段。说一个市场 mature，意味着它已停止疯狂扩张，找到了自己的形状。

senses.title: Finance: reach the date of payment
senses.definition: of a bond, policy, or loan, to reach the date on which the principal must be paid
senses.definitionCN: 指债券、保单或贷款到达必须偿付本金的日期
senses.example: The bond matures in ten years, but the interest is paid twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券十年后到期，但利息每年支付两次。
senses.why: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861. A debt, like fruit, has a fixed season: it is not paid early, but at the point when it has become 'due', from Latin maturus 'timely'.
senses.whyCN: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年。债务和果实一样有固定的季节：不提前偿付，而是在它“到期”的那一点——maturus 本义就是“及时的”。

senses.title: A polite word for older
senses.titleCN: 对“年纪较大”的委婉说法
senses.definition: used as a polite or euphemistic adjective for someone older than the usual age for a role
senses.definitionCN: 用作礼貌或委婉的形容词，指比某角色的通常年龄更大
senses.example: She returned to university as a mature student at forty.
senses.exampleCN: 她四十岁时以成年学生的身份重返大学。
senses.why: The euphemistic sense 'older than usual' is recorded by 1953. Instead of saying old, English says mature, borrowing the positive idea of full development to avoid the negative idea of decline.
senses.whyCN: “比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。英语不说 old，而说 mature，借“充分发展”的正面含义，避开“衰退”的负面含义。

senses.title: Usage boundary: mature, ripe, adult, old
senses.definition: mature is broader than ripe and more evaluative than adult; it describes full development, not age itself, so it is not a neutral synonym of old
senses.definitionCN: mature 比 ripe 更宽，比 adult 更具评价性；它描述充分发展，而不是年龄本身，因此不是 old 的中性同义词
senses.example: A mature person may be young; a ripe fruit is simply ready to eat.
senses.exampleCN: 成熟的人可能很年轻；熟透的果子只是到了能吃的时候。
senses.why: Ripe belongs to fruit and grain; adult belongs to legal or biological age; mature adds judgment, readiness, and the completion of a process. The euphemistic use for age shows how easily the positive sense can be borrowed for a different purpose.
senses.whyCN: ripe 属于果实与谷物；adult 属于法定或生理年龄；mature 再加上判断力、就绪状态与过程的完成。用它对年龄作委婉表达，正说明这个正面义项多么容易被借去服务另一个目的。

intro.en: Mature comes from Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early'. The word describes a process that has reached its proper point, and English extended it from fruit to people, plans, markets and debts. The deeper origin of maturus is not established.
intro.cn: mature 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”。这个词描述一个过程到达了它应有的节点，英语把它从果实扩展到人、计划、市场与债务。maturus 更深层的来源并未确立。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as maturen, 'encourage suppuration', then in the mid-15c. as 'cause to ripen, bring to maturity'. The earliest use is medical and agricultural, not moral.
items.cn: 动词最初记录为 maturen“促使化脓”，15 世纪中期转为“使成熟、带到成熟状态”。最早的用法是医学与农业的，而不是道德评价的。

items.en: The adjective appears of fruits, 'ripe, complete in natural growth or development', and of deliberations, 'careful, well-considered, thorough'.
items.cn: 形容词义出现，用于水果时意为“成熟的、自然生长或发育已完成的”，用于思考时意为“审慎的、周全的、彻底的”。

items.en: From Latin maturus 'ripe, timely, early', also the source of maturare 'to ripen, bring to maturity'. The link with mane 'early, of the morning' is standard.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的、早的”，也是 maturare“使成熟、带到成熟状态”的来源。它与 mane“早、清晨”的联系是通行说法。

items.en: The deeper origin of maturus is source uncertain. Some references cautiously connect it with a notion of 'ripeness' or with Latin manus 'good'; these are proposals, not established derivations, so no confident PIE root should be asserted.
items.cn: maturus 更深层的来源不确定。一些资料谨慎地把它与“成熟”的观念或拉丁语 manus“好”相联系；这些只是推测，不是已确立的派生关系，因此不应断言某个确定的原始印欧语词根。

items.en: Of persons, 'having fully developed powers of body and mind' is recorded c. 1600. The intransitive sense 'become ripe' follows in the 1650s.
items.cn: 用于人时，“身体与心智能力已充分发育”记录于约 1600 年。不及物义“变得成熟”随后在 17 世纪 50 年代出现。

items.en: The financial sense 'reach the time for payment' is recorded by 1861; the euphemistic sense 'older than usual' by 1953.
items.cn: 金融义“到达付款时间”记录于 1861 年；“比通常年龄更大”的委婉义记录于 1953 年。

note.en: The first group shares the maturus stem and its prefixes. The second group separates ripeness, legal adulthood, everyday grown-up behaviour and the softening that comes with age.
note.cn: 第一组共享 maturus 词干及其前缀。第二组区分果实成熟、法定成年、日常的“大人样”，以及随年龄而来的柔和。

entries.definition: the state of being mature, or the date when a financial product must be paid. It is the noun from mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成熟状态，或金融产品的到期日。它是 mature 的名词。

entries.definition: not fully developed, or behaving below the expected adult level. It adds the negative prefix in- to maturus.
entries.definitionCN: 未充分发育的，或行为低于成年人应有水平的。它在 maturus 前加了否定前缀 in-。

entries.definition: happening before the proper or expected time, as in a premature birth or a premature conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 在应有或预期时间之前发生的，如早产或过早的结论。

entries.definition: ready to be eaten or harvested, especially of fruit or grain. It is narrower and more physical than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 可以食用或收割的，尤指水果或谷物。它比 mature 更窄、更具体。

entries.definition: fully grown or legally of age. It marks a stage of life, while mature also judges behaviour and judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 发育完全或达到法定年龄。它标记人生阶段，而 mature 还评价行为与判断力。

entries.definition: adult, or behaving in an adult way. It is more conversational and less evaluative than mature.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的，或表现得像大人。它比 mature 更口语化，评价性更弱。

entries.definition: softened and pleasant with age, as of wine, sound, or a person. It stresses gentleness, while mature stresses completion.
entries.definitionCN: 随年龄变得柔和、悦人，如酒、声音或人。它强调温和，而 mature 强调完成。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maturus 'ripe, timely' gives mature, maturity, maturation, premature and immature; mane 'early' gives matins and matutinal.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：maturus“成熟的、及时的”给出 mature、maturity、maturation、premature、immature；mane“早”给出 matins、matutinal。

normal.en: Mature is a process word: something has reached the point it was growing toward. Fruit, wine, a person, a plan, a market and a bond can all arrive there.
normal.cn: mature 是一个过程词：某物到达了它一直生长所要到达的那一点。果实、酒、人、计划、市场、债券都可以到达那里。

normal.en: maturus means 'ripe' and also 'timely'. A mature bond is not old; it has simply reached its proper time.
normal.cn: maturus 既指“成熟”，也指“及时”。到期的债券不是“老”，它只是到达了它该到的时间。

normal.en: The verb first meant 'encourage suppuration' c. 1400: even an abscess was thought to come to a head in its own time. Ripening is a natural clock, not a push.
normal.cn: 动词约在 1400 年最早表示“促使化脓”：连脓肿也被认为会在自己的时间里“长熟”。成熟是一只自然的钟，不是硬推。

normal.en: The euphemism mature student (1953) borrows the positive sense of full development to avoid the word old.
normal.cn: mature student（1953）这个委婉说法，借“充分发展”的正面含义来避开 old 这个词。

normal.en: immature and premature are mature with a negative or a 'before' prefix: not yet developed, or developed too soon.
normal.cn: immature 与 premature 是给 mature 加上否定或“之前”的前缀：尚未发展，或发展得太早。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with no hands: you cannot see the time, only whether the fruit is still hard or finally soft. Mature is the moment the process says 'now'.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有指针的钟：你看不见时间，只能看见果子还是硬的、或终于软了。mature 就是过程说出“现在”的那一刻。

abstract.en: The same curve runs through a peach, a wine, a mind, a manuscript, an industry and a debt: slow completion, then readiness.
abstract.cn: 同一条曲线穿过桃子、酒、心智、手稿、产业与债务：缓慢完成，然后就绪。

abstract.en: What is mature is not old; it is finished enough to be used. Old age is only one of the places where that readiness can be seen.
abstract.cn: 成熟的东西不是“老”，而是“完成到可以使用”。年老只是这种就绪状态可能被看见的场所之一。

examples.en: The wine needs another five years to mature properly.
examples.cn: 这酒还需要再放五年才能好好成熟。

examples.en: He handled the criticism in a mature way.
examples.cn: 他以成熟的方式对待批评。

examples.en: The loan matures at the end of March.
examples.cn: 这笔贷款在三月底到期。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马球”——马球运动员等到果子熟了才开赛，说这是成熟的决定 → mature 成熟的

root: 拉丁语 maturus“成熟的、及时的”，核心是“过程走到应有的节点、可以用了”，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of mature, one ripening curve: ripe fruit, a grown person, adult judgment, a considered plan, the act of ripening, a settled market, a due debt, a polite word for older, and the boundary against ripe and old.
sensesIntro.cn: mature 的九个义项都是同一条成熟曲线：熟果、发育完全的人、成年人的判断、深思熟虑的计划、成熟的动作、稳定的市场、到期的债务、对年长的委婉说法，以及它与 ripe、old 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a process reaches its proper point, and what has grown is now ready.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个过程到达了应有的节点，长成的东西现在可以用了。

branches.en: FRUIT AND WINE: biological ripening is the literal source of the whole family.
branches.cn: 果实与酒：生物性的成熟是整个词族最字面的来源。

branches.en: PERSON: the body finishes growing, and behaviour is expected to finish growing too.
branches.cn: 人：身体完成生长，行为也被期待完成“长大”。

branches.en: PROCESS: a plan and a market both need time before they are ready to be used.
branches.cn: 过程：计划与市场都需要时间，才能就绪可用。

branches.en: FINANCE: a debt has a season, and maturing is reaching that date.
branches.cn: 金融：债务有它的季节，到期就是走到那个日期。

branches.en: EUPHEMISM AND BOUNDARY: age is softened by the positive sense, and mature never simply means old.
branches.cn: 委婉与边界：年龄被正面义项柔化，而 mature 从不简单等于 old。

intro.en: Mature takes Latin prefixes and English suffixes: im- and pre- negate or shift time, while -ity, -ly and -ation build nouns and adverbs. The stem matur- stays constant.
intro.cn: mature 接受拉丁前缀与英语后缀：im- 与 pre- 表示否定或时间偏移，-ity、-ly、-ation 构成名词与副词。词干 matur- 保持不变。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family joins maturus 'ripe, timely' with mane 'early, morning': matins and matutinal belong to the morning, while premature means ripening before its time.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族把 maturus“成熟的、及时的”与 mane“早、清晨”连在一起：matins 与 matutinal 属于清晨，premature 则指在时间之前就成熟。

items.meaning: the state of being fully developed; the date a financial product is due
items.meaningCN: 成熟；成熟期；到期（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The bond reaches maturity next year.

items.meaning: in a mature, calm, and considered way
items.meaningCN: 成熟地；深思熟虑地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She responded maturely to the criticism.
items.exampleCN: 她对批评作出了成熟的回应。

items.meaning: not fully developed, or not behaving at an adult level
items.meaningCN: 未成熟的；幼稚的（im- 表示否定）
items.example: The fruit is still immature and should be left on the tree.
items.exampleCN: 果子还没成熟，应该留在树上。

items.meaningCN: 过早的；早产的（pre- 表示“在……之前”）
items.example: It is premature to announce a result.
items.exampleCN: 现在宣布结果还为时过早。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source of mature.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是 mature 的直接来源。

items.example: The stem appears in mature, maturity and maturation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 mature、maturity 与 maturation。

items.example: It forms maturity, the state of being ripe.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturity，即成熟状态。

items.example: It forms maturation, the process of ripening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 maturation，即成熟过程。

items.meaning: the state of not being mature
items.example: The review criticized the immaturity of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 评审批评了这份计划的不成熟。

latinEntries.structure: Latin matutinus (of the morning) from mane (early)

latinEntries.meaning: the quality of happening or developing before the proper time
latinEntries.meaningCN: 过早；早产（在应有时间之前发生或发育的状态）

definition_en: to find out what illness or problem someone or something has
core_image: 医生把片子举到灯前，用笔尖点住那片阴影
scene: 医生把片子举到灯前，用笔尖轻轻点了点那片阴影。 The doctor diagnosed the illness as a rare infection.
sceneCN: 这里 diagnose 指「诊断」（第 1 个义项：判断出得的是什么病）；句意是医生诊断这种病是一种罕见的感染。

senses.title: Identify an illness
senses.definition: to find out what illness a person has by examining them
senses.definitionCN: 通过检查判断一个人得的是什么病
senses.example: The doctor diagnosed the illness as a rare infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生诊断这种病是一种罕见的感染。
senses.why: A name is the first medicine: once the enemy is known, the fight can start.
senses.whyCN: 名字是第一味药：敌人一旦被认出，仗就能打起来。

senses.title: Find the cause of a fault
senses.definition: to find out the cause of a problem in a machine or system
senses.definitionCN: 找出机器或系统中出现问题的原因
senses.example: Engineers diagnosed the fault in less than an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师不到一小时就判断出了故障所在。
senses.why: An engine cannot describe its pain, so someone must read the signs.
senses.whyCN: 发动机说不出哪里疼，只能由人去读那些迹象。

senses.title: Describe the nature of something
senses.definition: to state what something is after careful study
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细研究后说出某事物究竟是什么
senses.example: The report diagnosed the company's weakness as poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 报告判定这家公司的弱点是计划不周。
senses.why: The same eye that reads a body can read an organisation.
senses.whyCN: 能读懂身体的那双眼，也能读懂一个组织。

intro.en: Diagnose comes from Greek diagignoskein, to know thoroughly or tell apart, built from dia- and gignoskein, to know.
intro.cn: diagnose 来自希腊语 diagignoskein（彻底认识、分辨），由 dia- 与 gignoskein（知道）构成。

items.en: Gignoskein meant to know, and dia- added the sense of thorough separation.
items.cn: gignoskein 指知道，前缀 dia- 添上彻底分辨的意思。

items.en: Doctors used the word for telling one disease from another.
items.cn: 医生用它表示把一种病与另一种病分辨开来。

items.en: Medical Latin kept diagnosis as the name of that judgement.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语保留 diagnosis 作为这种判断的名称。

items.en: English diagnose appeared later, built back from diagnosis.
items.cn: 英语 diagnose 出现较晚，是从 diagnosis 反推造出的动词。

items.en: It now covers illnesses, machines, companies and whole systems.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖疾病、机器、公司以及整个系统。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- opening, while the meaning group moves from identifying to determining and detecting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dia- 开头，近义组则从辨认走到确定与察觉。

entries.definition: a judgement about what is wrong
used to find out what is wrong
running from one corner to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一个角连到另一个角的

entries.definition: to recognize what something is
to find out something exactly
to notice something hidden

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a film held up to a lamp and end with a report naming a company's weakness.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从举到灯前的片子开始，落到一份点出公司弱点的报告。

normal.en: Dia- means through, and knowing through a thing is diagnosis.
normal.cn: dia- 是穿过，把一件事看穿到底，就是诊断。

normal.en: The doctor does not guess; the doctor separates one cause from many.
normal.cn: 医生不猜，医生是从许多原因里把那个挑出来。

normal.en: An engine and a patient both answer only through signs.
normal.cn: 发动机与病人，都只通过迹象回答。

normal.en: A fault named is already half repaired.
normal.cn: 故障一旦被叫出名字，就已经修好了一半。

normal.en: The same word can read a body, a car or a company.
normal.cn: 同一个词，能读身体，也能读汽车与公司。

abstract.en: Picture a dark film glowing on a light box.
abstract.cn: 想象一张暗色片子在看片灯上发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a pen point resting on one grey shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象笔尖停在某一团灰色阴影上。

abstract.en: Picture a list of causes with one line underlined.
abstract.cn: 想象一张原因清单，其中一行被划了线。

root: 来自希腊语 diagignoskein，由 dia-（穿过、彻底）与 gignoskein（知道）组成，本义是把一种病与另一种病分辨清楚。经医学拉丁语进入英语，先有名词 diagnosis，再由它反推造出动词 diagnose，后来也用于判断机器、组织与制度的问题。

branches.en: The first sense is a name given to a body's trouble.

definition_zh: 繁荣；兴旺；成功；富足；顺境
definition_en: the condition of being successful and growing, especially when a country, region or business has rising income, trade and well-being
core_image: 粮仓一格格装满，账本上的数字连年往上走
scene: 港口重新修好的那几年，小城的码头上又挤满了货船，店铺一家接一家开张。 In the years after the harbour was rebuilt, prosperity returned to the little town.
sceneCN: 这里 prosperity 表示「经济繁荣、兴旺」（第 1 个义项：地区经济向上走）；句意为港口重建后的几年里，繁荣又回到了这座小城。

derivatives.zh: prosper 加 -ous 构成形容词，把「兴旺」写成一种性质
去掉后缀即得动词，意为「兴旺、发达」
prosperous 再加 -ly 构成副词，意为「兴旺地、富足地」

senses.title: Economic success and growth
senses.definition: the condition in which a country or region grows richer, with rising trade, income and employment
senses.definitionCN: 国家或地区越来越富裕，贸易、收入与就业都在上升的状态
senses.example: The port brought prosperity to the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口给整个地区带来了繁荣。
senses.why: Prosperity first names the visible sign of a hope that came true: warehouses full, ships coming in, wages paid. Because the Latin stem joins a forward direction to hope, the word naturally settles on growth you can see in a harbour or a market.
senses.whyCN: prosperity 最初指的是希望兑现之后看得见的迹象：仓库堆满、船只进港、工钱按时发放。它的拉丁词干把「朝前」和「希望」绑在一起，所以这个词自然落在港口与市场上看得见的增长。

senses.title: Personal success and good fortune
senses.definition: the state of doing well in one's life or career, with things going favourably
senses.definitionCN: 在人生或事业上走得顺，事情朝着有利方向发展的状态
senses.example: He attributed his prosperity to patience and a little luck.
senses.exampleCN: 他把自己的成功归功于耐心和一点运气。
senses.why: A hope placed in front of a country can also be placed in front of one person: when plans keep working out, the same word names a private run of good years rather than a national boom.
senses.whyCN: 放在一个国家前面的希望，也能放在一个人前面：当计划一件件走通，同一个词就从国家层面的景气转到私人生活里的一段好年景。

senses.title: A period of thriving
senses.definition: a stretch of years in which business and living standards are strong, seen as a period one can date
senses.definitionCN: 生意与生活水平都很强劲的一段年头，可以被标出起止时间
senses.example: The decades of prosperity ended abruptly with the war.
senses.exampleCN: 数十年的繁荣随着战争戛然而止。
senses.why: A boom has a beginning and an end, so the word can be counted and dated; it then names the years themselves, not a permanent condition.
senses.whyCN: 景气有开头也有结尾，所以这个词可以被计数、被标出年份；这时它指的是那几年本身，而不是一种永久状态。

senses.title: Material wealth; affluence
senses.definition: great wealth, especially as shown in comfortable living conditions and possessions
senses.definitionCN: 大量财富，尤指体现在舒适生活条件与财物上的富足
senses.example: They lived in prosperity, but never talked about money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们日子过得很富足，却从不谈钱。
senses.why: Seen through a household rather than a nation, the same state turns into furniture, food and leisure, so the word comes to mean the wealth itself rather than the growth that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 若从一户人家而不是一个国家的角度去看，同一种状态就变成家具、饭菜与闲暇，于是这个词指的是财富本身，而不是产生财富的那段增长。

senses.title: Favourable conditions; good fortune
senses.definition: favourable circumstances or good luck, especially in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 有利的境况或好运气，多见于较早或文学性的用法
senses.example: He wished them health and prosperity in the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 他祝他们来年健康顺遂。
senses.why: Before economics took the word over, it covered any favourable turn of events; the old blessing formula keeps that wider sense alive in toasts and greetings.
senses.whyCN: 在经济学接管这个词之前，它泛指任何有利的转折；祝酒与贺词里那套古老的祝福语，把这层更宽的意味保留了下来。

intro.en: Prosperity comes from Latin prosperitas, a noun built on prosperus, which is usually analysed as pro- 'forward' plus spes 'hope'.
intro.cn: prosperity 来自拉丁语 prosperitas，其基础是 prosperus；一般认为它由 pro-「向前」加 spes「希望」构成。

items.en: Spes meant hope. The picture behind it is a hope set in front of a person, something to walk toward.
items.cn: spes 意为希望。它背后的画面是把希望摆在人的前面，让人朝它走去。

items.en: Pro- (forward) plus spes gave prosperus, 'favourable, fortunate'. This is the usual analysis; the exact formation is still debated.
items.cn: pro-（向前）加 spes 得到 prosperus，意为「顺利的、吉利的」。这是通常的分析，但具体构词细节仍有讨论。

items.en: Prosperitas named favourable fortune and success, the abstract state behind the adjective.
items.cn: prosperitas 指顺遂的运气与成功，是把那个形容词变成抽象状态的名称。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prosperite, meaning success and well-being, and English took it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 prosperite，意为成功与安好，英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: Modern English prosperity covers national economies, private wealth and any run of good years.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prosperity 覆盖国家经济、私人财富以及任何一段顺遂的年头。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family around spes; the near-meaning group collects words for wealth and growth.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 spes 这一拉丁词族展开；近义组收表示财富与增长的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same stem, describing someone or something that is doing well.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干上的形容词，形容人或事物兴旺、发达。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to succeed or to do well, the base of both the noun and the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为兴旺、发达，是名词与形容词共同的词干。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in a successful or wealthy way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为兴旺地、富足地。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the quality of being prosperous.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的名词，指兴旺、富足的性质。

entries.definition: A large amount of money and possessions.
A period when trade and business grow quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 商业迅速增长的时期；景气。

entries.definition: The state of having plenty of money and comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财与舒适生活的状态；富足。

entries.definition: The achievement of a goal, or of fame and money.
entries.definitionCN: 达到目标，或获得名声与财富；成功。

normalIntro.en: Most of the word is carried by two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, and by the English suffixes that turn the verb prosper into a state.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词大半由两个拉丁成分撑起：pro- 与 spes，再加上把动词 prosper 变成状态名词的英语后缀。

normal.en: Pro- means forward and spes means hope, so prosperity is hope that has moved in front of you and come true.
normal.cn: pro- 是向前，spes 是希望，所以 prosperity 是「被放到你前面并且兑现了的希望」。

normal.en: Prosper is the verb underneath: a person prospers, and prosperity is the state that results.
normal.cn: 底下的动词是 prosper：人先兴旺起来，prosperity 是随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The suffix -ity turns an adjective into a state, the same way able becomes ability.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成状态，就像 able 变成 ability 一样。

normal.en: The Latin hope word spes also hides in desperate, where de- means without, so desperate is literally 'without hope'.
normal.cn: 拉丁语的希望 spes 还藏在 desperate 里：de- 表示「没有」，desperate 字面就是「没有希望」。

normal.en: Learn it inside the phrase economic prosperity, because the word is used most often about countries and regions.
normal.cn: 把它放在 economic prosperity 这个词组里记，因为它最常用来谈国家与地区。

abstract.en: Picture storehouses that are a little fuller each year: prosperity is the direction of the line, not a single good harvest.
abstract.cn: 想象一排粮仓，每年都比上一年满一点：繁荣是那条线的方向，而不是一次好收成。

abstract.en: A boom can end, so the word often takes a period word beside it, as in a decade of prosperity.
abstract.cn: 景气会结束，所以这个词旁边常带一个表示时间段的词，例如十年繁荣。

abstract.en: Shared prosperity asks whether the growth reaches ordinary tables, which is why the phrase carries moral weight.
abstract.cn: 共享繁荣问的是增长有没有落到普通人的餐桌上，这也是这个说法带有道德分量的原因。

examples.en: The new railway brought prosperity to villages that had been cut off for centuries.
examples.cn: 新铁路给那些与外界隔绝了几个世纪的村庄带来了繁荣。

examples.en: Economists still argue about how long the present prosperity can last.
examples.cn: 经济学家仍在争论当前的繁荣能持续多久。

examples.en: His prosperity began with a small workshop behind the family house.
examples.cn: 他的兴旺始于自家屋后的一间小作坊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「铺路拾贝提」：先把路铺好，再拾到贝壳，最后提到货，一路忙下来，家业就兴旺了。

root: 拉丁语 pro（向前）+ spes（希望）构成 prosperus（顺遂的、吉利的），其名词 prosperitas 经古法语 prosperite 进入英语。一般认为这一词源分析成立，但 prosperus 的具体构词仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hoped-for turn that really goes well; from that one idea grow economic boom, personal success, a dated period of good years, material comfort and the older sense of good fortune.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「盼来的转机真的变好」；由这一个念头长出经济繁荣、个人成功、可数的一段好年景、物质富足，以及较早的「好运、顺境」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: granaries filling up year after year while the ledger totals climb.
core.cn: 核心意象：粮仓一年比一年满，账本上的总数不断往上走。

branches.en: a harbour where loaded ships keep arriving and wages are paid on time
branches.cn: 货船不断进港、工钱按时发放的港口

branches.en: a man reading a good annual report at his desk
branches.cn: 一个人坐在桌前读一份漂亮的年报

branches.en: a stretch of good years marked on a timeline
branches.cn: 时间轴上被标出的一段好年头

branches.en: a warm house with a full table
branches.cn: 桌上摆满饭菜的暖屋子

branches.en: a New Year toast raised in a hall
branches.cn: 大厅里举起的祝酒

intro.en: Two Latin pieces, pro- and spes, plus a noun suffix explain how a hope becomes a verb, a state and a description.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁成分 pro- 与 spes，加上名词后缀，解释了「希望」如何变成动词、状态名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around spes is well recorded: a noun for hope, a verb for hoping, and the prosperus words for good fortune.
latinIntro.cn: spes 周围的拉丁词族有清楚记录：表示希望的名词、表示期盼的动词，以及表示好运的 prosperus 一族。

items.example: The small firm began to prosper.
items.exampleCN: 这家小公司开始兴旺起来。

definition_zh: 繁荣；挥动；花饰；夸张动作
definition_en: to grow or succeed well, to wave something in the air, or a showy decorative movement
core_image: 乐手把琴弓向上一挑，收在一个漂亮的动作里
scene: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。 The small business flourished in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 flourish 是「兴旺」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小生意在城里兴旺起来。

senses.title: Grow well
senses.definition: to grow strongly and healthily
senses.definitionCN: 茁壮而健康地生长
senses.example: The plants flourish in warm rain.
senses.exampleCN: 植物在暖雨中长得茂盛。
senses.why: This is the original sense of flowering.
senses.whyCN: 这是开花的本义。

senses.title: Succeed
senses.definition: to be successful or active
senses.definitionCN: 成功或活跃地发展
senses.example: The small business flourished in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 小生意在城里兴旺起来。
senses.why: A growing plant became a metaphor for success.
senses.whyCN: 生长的植物被隐喻为成功。

senses.title: Wave
senses.definition: to hold something up and move it about
senses.definitionCN: 举起某物并来回挥动
senses.example: He flourished the letter in triumph.
senses.exampleCN: 他得意地挥动那封信。
senses.why: A showy gesture is like a plant waving in the air.
senses.whyCN: 夸张的手势像植物在空中摆动。

senses.title: Decorative movement
senses.definition: a showy curve or gesture added for effect
senses.definitionCN: 为效果添加的夸张曲线或动作
senses.example: She signed with a flourish.
senses.exampleCN: 她签名时带了一个花饰。
senses.why: The noun names the flourish of a pen or hand.
senses.whyCN: 名词指笔或手的华彩动作。

note.en: Flourish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for thriving.

intro.en: Dormitory comes from Latin dormitorium, a sleeping place, built on dormire, to sleep.
intro.cn: dormitory 来自拉丁语 dormitorium（睡觉的地方），其根为 dormire（睡）。

items.en: Dormire meant to sleep and supplied the verb root for the whole family.
items.cn: dormire 意为「睡觉」，为整族词提供动词词根。

items.en: Dormitorium named a sleeping room, especially a shared one in a monastery.
items.cn: dormitorium 指睡房，尤指修道院里共用的寝室。

items.en: The word entered English for a shared sleeping room in religious houses.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，先指宗教团体里共用的寝室。

items.en: Schools and universities used it for large buildings that housed many students.

items.en: British planners applied it to dormitory towns and suburbs where people only sleep.
items.cn: 英国规划者把它用到人们只在此睡觉的睡城与郊区。

definition_en: the line that marks the outer edge of a shape; a short account of the main points of something; and the verbs for drawing that edge or for summarizing those points
core_image: 铅笔沿着影子的边缘走了一圈，纸上只剩一条线
scene: 夜里灯从侧面照过来，墙上落下一个人的影子，孩子拿铅笔沿着影子的边慢慢描。 He drew the outline of his hand on the paper.
sceneCN: 这里是「轮廓、外形」（第 1 个义项：描出物体外缘的那条线）；句意为他在纸上描出自己手的轮廓。图中可辨识物件：侧照的灯、墙上的影子、铅笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 outline 加 -ed 构成，义为「有轮廓的；带描边的」

senses.title: The line marking the outer edge
senses.definition: the line that marks the outer edge of a shape or object, especially as seen against a background
senses.definitionCN: 标出一个形状或物体外缘的线，尤指在背景衬托下看到的
senses.example: He drew the outline of his hand on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他在纸上描出自己手的轮廓。
senses.why: Out plus line gives a line that travels around the outside of a thing, so the noun begins as the visible boundary of a shape rather than anything inside it.
senses.whyCN: out 加 line 就是「沿外面走的那条线」，所以这个名词最初指一个形状看得见的外缘，而不是它内部的东西。

senses.title: A summary of the main points
senses.definition: a short description or plan that gives the main points of something without the supporting details
senses.definitionCN: 只给要点、不含细节的简短说明或方案
senses.example: She wrote an outline before starting the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她动笔写文章之前先列了提纲。
senses.why: If a line can mark the edge of a shape, a line of argument can mark the edge of a subject, so the word came to mean the bare frame of a text or a plan.
senses.whyCN: 既然一条线可以标出一个形状的边，一串论点也可以标出一个题目的边，于是这个词转而指文章或方案最简的骨架。

senses.title: To draw the outer edge of something
senses.definition: to draw or trace the outer edge of a shape, usually with a single continuous line
senses.definitionCN: 用线条描出一个形状的外缘，通常只画一条连续的线
senses.example: The map outlines the coast in fine black ink.
senses.exampleCN: 地图用细细的黑线勾出海岸的轮廓。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without changing its picture: to outline is to make the very line the noun names, so the action and its result share one image.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词时画面没变：to outline 就是画出名词所指的那条线，于是动作和结果共用同一个图像。

senses.title: To describe something in general terms
senses.definition: to give the main points of a plan, idea or argument without going into detail
senses.definitionCN: 只讲计划、想法或论述的要点，不深入细节
senses.example: The manager outlined the changes at the morning meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 经理在晨会上概述了这些变动。
senses.why: From drawing the edge of a shape, the verb moves to marking the edge of a subject, which is exactly what a summary does: it traces the boundary and leaves the interior blank.
senses.whyCN: 从描出一个形状的边，这个动词转到标出一个题目的边，而概括做的正是这件事：把边界走一遍，把里面留空。

intro.en: Outline is an English compound of out and line, and line itself goes back through French to Latin linea, a thread of linen used for measuring.
intro.cn: outline 是 out 与 line 的英语复合词，而 line 本身经法语可追到拉丁语 linea，指用来量长短的亚麻线。

items.en: Linea meant a line, a string or a linen thread, and it is the source of the English word line.
items.cn: linea 意为线、绳或亚麻线，是英语 line 的来源。

items.en: Old French ligne carried the Latin word into English with the sense of a drawn line or a boundary.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 把拉丁词带进英语，意思是一条画出的线或一条边界。

items.en: English joined out and line to name the boundary line of a figure, seen against the space around it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语把 out 与 line 合起来，指图形与周围空间相接的那条边界线。

items.en: The same noun was applied to a sketch containing only contours and then to a summary of the main points of a text.
items.cn: 同一个名词先被用于只含轮廓的草图，随后又指文章要点的摘要。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb, and uses outline in course outlines, project outlines and the phrase in outline.
items.cn: 现代英语又添出动词用法，并把 outline 用在课程大纲、项目提纲以及 in outline 这个说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the out compound and the line family; the near-meaning group collects words for shapes seen from outside and for short summaries.
note.cn: 形近组收 out 复合词与 line 词族；近义组收表示「从外面看到的形状」以及简短摘要的词。

senses.example: She kept the whole secret in a selfish way.
senses.exampleCN: 她自私地把整个秘密藏在心里。
senses.why: Failure to share is a common form of selfishness.
senses.whyCN: 不愿分享是自私的常见表现。

senses.title: Motivated by self-interest
senses.definition: done mainly for your own advantage
senses.definitionCN: 主要为了自己的好处而做
senses.example: He helped only for selfish reasons.
senses.exampleCN: 他帮忙只是出于私利。
senses.why: An act can be selfish without being cruel.
senses.whyCN: 一个行为可以自私，却未必残忍。

intro.en: Selfish joins self, one's own person, with the adjective suffix -ish.
intro.cn: selfish 由 self（自身）加形容词后缀 -ish 构成。

items.en: Self named the same person.
items.cn: self 指同一个人自身。

items.en: The suffix -ish formed adjectives from nouns.
items.cn: 后缀 -ish 由名词构成形容词。

items.en: Selfish appeared in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: selfish 在十七世纪出现。

items.en: The word described conduct and motives.
items.cn: 该词用来形容行为与动机。

items.en: Biology produced the phrase selfish gene.
items.cn: 生物学产生了「自私的基因」这一说法。

note.en: Selfish is compared with similar-looking words and with words for self-centred behaviour.
note.cn: 把 selfish 与形近词以及表示以自我为中心的词作比较。

entries.definition: the person you are
caring more for others
the quality of being selfish

normalIntro.en: Selfish describes someone who thinks mainly about themselves.
normalIntro.cn: selfish 形容一个人主要只想着自己。

normal.en: Self plus the suffix -ish makes selfish.
normal.cn: self 加上后缀 -ish 就是 selfish。

normal.en: The opposite is selfless.
normal.cn: 反义词是 selfless。

normal.en: A selfish act takes without sharing.
normal.cn: 自私的行为只取不予。

normal.en: The noun is selfishness.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 selfishness。

normal.en: A selfish person forgets who else is at the table.
normal.cn: 自私的人会忘记桌旁还有别人。

abstract.en: Selfishness narrows the world to one pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 自私把世界缩小到一双眼睛。

abstract.en: What looks selfish may hide fear.
abstract.cn: 看似自私的行为，也许藏着恐惧。

abstract.en: Sharing is a choice made against selfishness every day.
abstract.cn: 分享是每天对抗自私的选择。

examples.en: It was selfish of him to take the last piece.
examples.cn: 他拿走最后一块，真是太自私了。

examples.en: He helped only for selfish reasons.
examples.cn: 他帮忙只是出于私利。

examples.en: Selfish behaviour costs friendships.
examples.cn: 自私行为会损害友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: selfish 由 self（自我）加 -ish（带有……性质的）构成，意为「只想着自己的」，反义词为 selfless。

root: 由 self（自身）加后缀 -ish 构成，核心义「带有只顾自身性质的」。

sensesIntro.en: Selfish means caring only about oneself, unwilling to share, or driven by self-interest.
sensesIntro.cn: selfish 意为只顾自己、不愿分享或出于私利的。

core.en: A heart turned toward itself alone.
core.cn: 只朝向自己的那颗心。

branches.en: My needs come before yours.
branches.cn: 我的需要排在你的前面。

branches.en: Nothing is given away.
branches.cn: 什么都不愿让出去。

branches.en: A kind act serves only me.
branches.cn: 看似好意，实则只为自己。

branches.en: Putting oneself first often means not sharing.
branches.cn: 把自己放第一位，往往就不肯分享。

branches.en: Self-interest drives both habits and motives.
branches.cn: 私利同时驱动习惯与动机。

intro.en: Selfish sits in a family of self compounds and opposites.
intro.cn: selfish 处于一组 self 复合词与反义词之中。

latinIntro.en: The base self is Germanic, so there are no Latin base forms to add.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 self 属日耳曼语，没有对应的拉丁语词根条目。

items.exampleCN: 他把自我放在家庭之前。

definition_en: to remove something from a surface, read quickly, or move lightly over
core_image: 石子在水面上轻轻掠过，留下几圈波纹
scene: 他快速浏览报纸，寻找那场比赛的消息。 He skimmed the newspaper for news of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 skim 是「快速浏览」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他快速浏览报纸，寻找那场比赛的消息。

senses.title: Remove from the surface
senses.definition: to remove something floating on the surface of a liquid
senses.definitionCN: 把漂浮在液体表面的东西去掉
senses.example: She skimmed the fat from the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她撇去汤面上的油脂。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义项。

senses.title: Read quickly
senses.definition: to read something quickly to get the main idea
senses.definitionCN: 快速阅读以了解主要内容
senses.example: He skimmed the newspaper for news of the match.
senses.exampleCN: 他快速浏览报纸，寻找那场比赛的消息。
senses.why: The eyes move lightly over the page like a hand over water.
senses.whyCN: 目光轻掠纸面，就像手掠过水面。

senses.title: Move lightly over
senses.definition: to move quickly and lightly over or near a surface
senses.definitionCN: 快速而轻地掠过或靠近表面移动
senses.example: A swallow skimmed the surface of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 一只燕子掠过湖面。
senses.why: The motion sense connects the other two.
senses.whyCN: 移动义把另外两个义项连接起来。

intro.en: Skim probably came from an Old French word for removing foam.
intro.cn: skim 可能来自古法语中表示撇去泡沫的词。

items.en: Escumer meant to remove scum.
items.cn: escumer 意为撇去浮沫。

items.en: The word appeared as skimmen.
items.cn: 这个词以 skimmen 的形式出现。

items.en: The spelling became skim.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 skim。

items.en: Reading quickly took the same word.
items.cn: 快速阅读也用了同一个词。

items.en: Light movement over water kept the image.
items.cn: 掠水的轻快移动保留了这一意象。

note.en: Skim is compared with look-alike words and words for quick reading.
note.cn: 把 skim 与形近词以及表示快速阅读的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Skim means touching only the top and moving on.
normalIntro.cn: skim 意为只碰到最上面就继续前进。

normal.en: He skimmed the newspaper for news of the match.
normal.cn: 他快速浏览报纸，寻找那场比赛的消息。

normal.en: She skimmed the fat from the soup.
normal.cn: 她撇去汤面上的油脂。

normal.en: A swallow skimmed the surface of the lake.
normal.cn: 一只燕子掠过湖面。

normal.en: I only skimmed the report before the meeting.
normal.cn: 开会前我只粗略看了报告。

normal.en: A flat stone can skim across the water.
normal.cn: 一块扁石头能掠过水面。

abstract.en: To skim is to trust the surface for a moment.
abstract.cn: 快速浏览就是暂且相信表面。

abstract.en: Some days ask for depth, others for a quick skim.
abstract.cn: 有些日子需要深入，有些只需略读。

abstract.en: Light touches can still tell you where to dive.
abstract.cn: 轻轻一触也能告诉你该在哪里潜入。

sensesIntro.en: Skim covers removing surface matter, reading fast, and moving lightly over a surface.
sensesIntro.cn: skim 涵盖撇去表面物、快速阅读以及轻掠表面。

core.en: A light movement across the top of something.
core.cn: 在物体顶部轻轻掠过。

branches.en: A spoon lifts foam from the top.
branches.cn: 勺子从上面撇起浮沫。

branches.en: Eyes run over lines without stopping.
branches.cn: 目光在行间奔过而不停留。

branches.en: A bird touches the water and rises.
branches.cn: 鸟碰到水面又升起。

branches.en: Both removing and gliding stay at the surface.
branches.cn: 撇去和滑行都停留在表面。

branches.en: Reading and flight share a quick light motion.
branches.cn: 阅读与飞行共享一种轻快的动作。

intro.en: Skim forms a few words about surfaces and quick reading.
intro.cn: skim 构成几个与表面和快速阅读有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Skim probably came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: skim 可能经古法语传入。

She skimmed the page in seconds.
items.exampleCN: 她几秒钟就看完了这一页。

items.example: Skimming is useful before a lecture.
items.exampleCN: 听讲座前浏览一下很有用。
